cols.EXTENT_COMPETED: How much competition there was for the contract, in words, like FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION or NOT COMPETED.

cols.RESEARCH: The small-business research program and phase in words, like SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH PROGRAM PHASE II ACTION. Almost always blank.

cols.FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES: Why an order under an existing contract was or was not opened to other holders, in words, like FAIR OPPORTUNITY GIVEN or URGENCY.

cols.CLINGER_COHEN_ACT_PLANNING: Whether the tech buy followed federal IT planning rules, as YES or NO.

cols.INTERAGENCY_CONTRACTING_AUTHORITY: The law that let one agency buy for another, in words, like ECONOMY ACT, OTHER STATUTORY AUTHORITY or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.OTHER_STATUTORY_AUTHORITY: The law cited when one agency bought for another under something other than the Economy Act, as free text like 40 U.S.C. 321. Almost always blank.
cols.PROGRAM_ACRONYM: The short name of the government-wide contract program used, like SEWP V or GWAC-VETS 2. Almost always blank.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_TYPE_CODE: A short code for the type of umbrella contract this order was placed under, like A, B or C. The words for it are in PARENT_AWARD_TYPE.

cols.PARENT_AWARD_SINGLE_OR_MULTIPLE: Whether the umbrella contract went to one company or several: SINGLE AWARD or MULTIPLE AWARD.

cols.USASPENDING_PERMALINK: A web link to this award's page on usaspending.gov.
cols.INITIAL_REPORT_DATE: When the transaction was first reported to the federal spending system.
cols.LAST_MODIFIED_DATE: When the source last changed this record. Some tables add the time.

cols.CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's own key for the whole contract, built from the contract number and agency code, like CONT_AWD_FA527023F0101_9700.
cols.AWARD_ID_PIID: The government's contract number, like FA527023F0101.
cols.ACTION_DATE: The date of the award action, like a new contract or a change to one. Two tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_START_DATE: The date the work or grant was set to begin. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_CURRENT_END_DATE: The date the work or grant is currently set to end, which can be in the future. Some tables store it as text.
cols.FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION: The dollars the government committed or took back in this one transaction. Negative numbers are cuts or cancellations.
cols.TOTAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED: The total dollars the government has committed to the whole contract so far, across all its transactions. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.CURRENT_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: What the whole contract is currently worth in dollars, counting options already used. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency that made the award, like Department of Defense.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The office inside the agency that gave the award, like Department of the Navy or National Park Service.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency whose money paid for the award. Can differ from the agency that made it.
cols.RECIPIENT_UEI: The recipient's 12-character federal ID, the Unique Entity ID that replaced the DUNS number.
cols.RECIPIENT_DUNS: The recipient's old 9-digit DUNS business number. 000000000 means none, and newer tables leave it empty.
cols.CAGE_CODE: The contractor's five-character Defense Department vendor code, like 1L027. Blank for many rows in some tables.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency, or campaign.
cols.RECIPIENT_DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The trade name the contractor goes by, if different from its legal name. Blank for most rows.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal ID of the recipient's parent company. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, in capitals. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY_NAME: The city where the recipient is based, in capitals.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_CODE: The recipient's state, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_4_CODE: The contractor's full nine-digit zip code, usually with no dash. Leading zeros can be lost.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_NAME: The country where the recipient is based, in capitals. The US shows up as both UNITED STATES and UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_CODE: The state where the work was actually done, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CITY_NAME: The city where the work was actually done, in capitals. Can differ from where the recipient is based.
cols.AWARD_TYPE: What kind of award: a contract type like PURCHASE ORDER or DELIVERY ORDER, or a grant type. Some rows use short forms like PO or DO, and the NIH table uses a one-digit code.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The six-digit industry code, like 722110 for restaurants. Needs a lookup to read; 000000 means not given.
cols.NAICS_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, like Full-Service Restaurants. It goes with the six-digit NAICS code.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE_DESCRIPTION: What kind of thing the government bought, in capitals, like OFFICE SUPPLIES or DRUGS AND BIOLOGICALS.
cols.TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: A free-text note on what was bought or funded, often full of internal codes and abbreviations.

cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_1_AMOUNT: The yearly pay in dollars of the recipient's top-paid executive.

cols.HIGHLY_COMPENSATED_OFFICER_2_AMOUNT: The yearly pay in dollars of the recipient's second top-paid executive.

cols.FRS_ID: The EPA's 12-digit facility registry number, starting 110.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site, or building, as the agency wrote it.
cols.CITY: The city or town name. Mostly in capitals, sometimes mixed case, and spellings are not cleaned.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY: The county name, without the word County. Mostly U.S. counties, but the UK company table holds UK counties.
cols.FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit number code, like 36089. Stored as text so leading zeros survive.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, in decimal degrees. U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.EPA_REGION: The EPA region number, 01 to 10, stored as two-digit text.
cols.PCT_MINORITY: The percent of people nearby, or living in the housing project, who are minorities, like 33.7. The HUD table stores it as text and has bad values like -4.
cols.POPULATION_DENSITY: People per square mile around the facility. Often blank.
cols.COMPLIANCE_STATUS: The facility's current rule-breaking status, in words, from No Violation Identified up to Significant Violation.
cols.QUARTERS_WITH_NONCOMPLIANCE: How many of the last 12 quarters the facility was out of compliance, 0 to 12.
cols.TOTAL_INSPECTION_COUNT: How many inspections the facility has had.
cols.FORMAL_ACTION_COUNT: How many formal enforcement actions were taken against the facility.
cols.TOTAL_PENALTIES: Total dollars in penalties against the facility. 0 means none.
cols.LAST_PENALTY_AMT: The dollar amount of the most recent penalty. If that case covered many facilities, this is the whole case amount.
cols.LAST_PENALTY_AMT_ALLOCATED: This facility's share of the most recent penalty, in dollars: the case total split across the facilities it covered.
cols.LAST_PENALTY_SHARED_FACILITY_N: How many facilities shared the most recent penalty. One value, 3013568, is far too big and looks like a no-penalty filler.
cols.DATE_LAST_INSPECTION: The date of the facility's most recent inspection. Often blank.
cols.DATE_LAST_FORMAL_ACTION: The date of the most recent formal enforcement action. Mostly blank.
cols.HAS_AIR_PROGRAM: True if the facility is regulated under the air pollution program.
cols.HAS_WATER_PROGRAM: True if the facility is regulated under the water pollution program.
cols.HAS_HAZWASTE_PROGRAM: True if the facility is regulated under the hazardous waste program.
cols.TRI_ON_SITE_RELEASES: Pounds of toxic chemicals the facility reported releasing on site. Almost always blank.

cols.PGM_SYS_ACRNM: The short name of the EPA database the record comes from, like ICIS, RCRAINFO, or TRIS.

cols.UNIT_OF_MEASURE: The unit the amount is measured in, like Pounds or mg/L.

cols.INFOTABLE_SK: The SEC's row number for one holding line in a 13F report.
cols.NAMEOFISSUER: The name of the company whose stock is held, like APPLE INC.
cols.TITLEOFCLASS: The kind of stock held, like COM for common stock or CL A for class A shares.
cols.CUSIP: The 9-character ID of the stock or bond, letters and digits.
cols.FIGI: An open-standard ID for the stock.
cols.VALUE_COL: A dollar value: what the stock holding or gift was worth. Stored as text; the gift table is messy, like HE or $2,400.00.
cols.SSHPRNAMT: How many shares are held, or the dollar face amount if the holding is a bond. The next column says which.
cols.SSHPRNAMTTYPE: Whether the amount column counts shares, SH, or bond dollars, PRN.
cols.PUTCALL: Put or Call if the holding is an option on the stock. Almost always blank, meaning plain stock.
cols.INVESTMENTDISCRETION: Who decides trades on the holding: SOLE for the filer alone, DFND for shared with others, OTR for other.
cols.OTHERMANAGER: The number of another money manager who shares the holding, as listed in the filing. Often blank.
cols.VOTING_AUTH_SOLE: How many of the shares the filer alone can vote. A number stored as text.
cols.VOTING_AUTH_SHARED: How many of the shares the filer votes together with others. A number stored as text; mostly 0.
cols.VOTING_AUTH_NONE: How many of the shares the filer has no vote on. A number stored as text.

cols.ACCESSION_NUMBER: The SEC's unique number for one filing, like 0001193125-24-036425.
cols.FILING_DATE: The date the filing was made. Watch out: one SEC table stores it as text like 31-AUG-2022, and two others show year 0026 when they mean 2026.
cols.CIK: The company's SEC filer number. Some tables pad it to 10 digits with leading zeros and some do not, so strip zeros before matching.

cols.REGISTRANT_NAME: The name of whoever registered, like a lobbying firm, fund, foreign agent, aircraft owner, or offender. People are often last name first.

cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros survive. Some are 5 digits, some 9 with or without a dash.

cols.PROVIDER_TYPE_CODE: Medicare's code for the kind of provider, like 00-09 for a hospital. Each table mostly holds one value.
cols.PROVIDER_TYPE_TEXT: The kind of provider in words, like PART A PROVIDER - HOSPITAL.
cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit Medicare provider number, the National Provider Identifier. Stored as text.
cols.MULTIPLE_NPI_FLAG: Y if this enrollment covers more than one provider number, N if not.
cols.CCN: The facility's 6-character Medicare certification number. Stored as text; some hold letters, like 37T056.
cols.ASSOCIATE_ID: Medicare's 10-digit ID for the enrolled organization, used to link its enrollments and owners. Stored as text; a few look short, like lost leading zeros.
cols.ORGANIZATION_NAME: The name of the organization, like a charity, clinic, or home health agency.
cols.DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The name the facility operates under, when it differs from its legal name. Often empty.
cols.INCORPORATION_DATE: The date the company or organization was legally formed.
cols.INCORPORATION_STATE: The state where the organization is legally formed, as two letters. Often empty.
cols.ORGANIZATION_TYPE_STRUCTURE: The organization's legal form: CORPORATION, LLC, PARTNERSHIP, SOLE PROPRIETOR, or OTHER.
cols.ORGANIZATION_OTHER_TYPE_TEXT: A free-text description of the legal form when it is OTHER, like COUNTY OWNED or 501C3. Empty for most rows.
cols.PROPRIETARY_NONPROFIT: Whether the facility is for-profit or non-profit: P for for-profit, N for non-profit. Some tables also have D.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the street address, like 13 STATION ROAD.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second address line, usually a suite or floor. Often empty.
cols.CITY: The city or town name. Mostly in capitals, sometimes mixed case, and spellings are not cleaned.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros survive. Some are 5 digits, some 9 with or without a dash.
cols.PRACTICE_LOCATION_TYPE: What kind of site this address is, like MAIN/PRIMARY HOSPITAL LOCATION or HHA BRANCH. Often blank.
cols.LOCATION_OTHER_TYPE_TEXT: Free-text site type when the listed types did not fit. Almost always blank.

cols.CCN: The facility's 6-character Medicare certification number. Stored as text; some hold letters, like 37T056.
cols.FACILITY_NAME: The name of the plant, site, or building, as the agency wrote it.
cols.ADDRESS: The full address in one line of text. Formats are messy and not split into parts.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros survive. Some are 5 digits, some 9 with or without a dash.
cols.COUNTY_PARISH: The county name, or parish in Louisiana. Casing varies.
cols.TELEPHONE_NUMBER: The facility's phone number. Some tables write it with the area code in brackets and a dash, others store bare digits.
cols.HOSPITAL_TYPE: The kind of hospital, like Acute Care Hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals or Psychiatric.
cols.HOSPITAL_OWNERSHIP: Who owns the hospital, like Proprietary for for-profit, Voluntary non-profit, or a level of government.
cols.EMERGENCY_SERVICES: Whether the hospital has an emergency room, Yes or No.
cols.MEETS_CRITERIA_FOR_BIRTHING_FRIENDLY_DES: Y if the hospital earned Medicare's birthing-friendly label. Blank otherwise.
cols.HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING: Medicare's star rating for the hospital, 1 to 5. Often blank.
cols.HOSPITAL_OVERALL_RATING_FOOTNOTE: A footnote number explaining a missing or odd star rating. Needs the CMS footnote list to read.
cols.MORT_GROUP_MEASURE_COUNT: How many death-rate measures go into the star rating. Always 8.
cols.COUNT_OF_FACILITY_MORT_MEASURES: How many of the death-rate measures the hospital has scores for.
cols.COUNT_OF_MORT_MEASURES_BETTER: How many death-rate measures the hospital beat the national rate on.
cols.COUNT_OF_MORT_MEASURES_NO_DIFFERENT: How many death-rate measures the hospital matched the national rate on.
cols.COUNT_OF_MORT_MEASURES_WORSE: How many death-rate measures the hospital did worse than the national rate on.
cols.MORT_GROUP_FOOTNOTE: A footnote number on the death-rate group. Needs the CMS footnote list to read. Mostly blank.
cols.SAFETY_GROUP_MEASURE_COUNT: How many patient-safety measures go into the star rating. Always 8.
cols.COUNT_OF_FACILITY_SAFETY_MEASURES: How many of the patient-safety measures the hospital has scores for.
cols.COUNT_OF_SAFETY_MEASURES_BETTER: How many patient-safety measures the hospital beat the national rate on.
cols.COUNT_OF_SAFETY_MEASURES_NO_DIFFERENT: How many patient-safety measures the hospital matched the national rate on.
cols.COUNT_OF_SAFETY_MEASURES_WORSE: How many patient-safety measures the hospital did worse than the national rate on.
cols.SAFETY_GROUP_FOOTNOTE: A footnote number on the patient-safety group. Needs the CMS footnote list to read. Mostly blank.
cols.READM_GROUP_MEASURE_COUNT: How many hospital-return measures, patients coming back after discharge, go into the star rating. Always 11.
cols.COUNT_OF_FACILITY_READM_MEASURES: How many of the hospital-return measures the hospital has scores for.
cols.COUNT_OF_READM_MEASURES_BETTER: How many hospital-return measures the hospital beat the national rate on.
cols.COUNT_OF_READM_MEASURES_NO_DIFFERENT: How many hospital-return measures the hospital matched the national rate on.
cols.COUNT_OF_READM_MEASURES_WORSE: How many hospital-return measures the hospital did worse than the national rate on.
cols.READM_GROUP_FOOTNOTE: A footnote number on the hospital-return group. Needs the CMS footnote list to read. Mostly blank.
cols.PT_EXP_GROUP_MEASURE_COUNT: How many patient-survey measures go into the star rating. Always 15.
cols.COUNT_OF_FACILITY_PT_EXP_MEASURES: How many of the patient-survey measures the hospital has scores for: 5, 10 or 15.
cols.PT_EXP_GROUP_FOOTNOTE: A footnote number on the patient-survey group. Needs the CMS footnote list to read. Mostly blank.
cols.TE_GROUP_MEASURE_COUNT: How many timely-and-effective-care measures go into the star rating. Always 10.
cols.COUNT_OF_FACILITY_TE_MEASURES: How many of the timely-and-effective-care measures the hospital has scores for.
cols.TE_GROUP_FOOTNOTE: A footnote number on the timely-and-effective-care group. Needs the CMS footnote list to read. Mostly blank.

cols.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN: The nursing home's six-digit Medicare ID. Kept as text so leading zeros like 015073 survive.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001. Stored as text so leading zeros survive.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros survive. Some are 5 digits, some 9 with or without a dash.
cols.OWNERSHIP_TYPE: Who owns it: for-profit, non-profit, government, cooperative, and so on. Wording differs by table.
cols.ADDRESS: The full address in one line of text. Formats are messy and not split into parts.
cols.CITY: The city or town name. Mostly in capitals, sometimes mixed case, and spellings are not cleaned.
cols.COUNTY_PARISH: The county name, or parish in Louisiana. Casing varies.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, in decimal degrees. U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.PHONE_NUMBER: A phone number, typed in mixed formats: with or without dashes, and with country codes for foreign numbers. Blank for many rows.
cols.DATE_FIRST_APPROVED_TO_PROVIDE_MEDICARE_: The date the nursing home was first approved to take Medicare and Medicaid patients.
cols.PROCESSING_DATE: The date CMS put out this batch of the file. The same date on every row of a table.
cols.PROVIDER_RESIDES_IN_HOSPITAL: Whether the nursing home is inside a hospital, Y or N.
cols.CONTINUING_CARE_RETIREMENT_COMMUNITY: Whether the nursing home is part of a retirement community with several levels of care, Y or N.
cols.SPECIAL_FOCUS_STATUS: Whether CMS put the nursing home on its watch list for homes with a record of serious problems: SFF means on it, SFF Candidate means in line for it. Blank for about 96% of homes.
cols.ABUSE_ICON: Y if the nursing home is marked with CMS's abuse warning icon, N if not.
cols.MOST_RECENT_HEALTH_INSPECTION_MORE_THAN_: Y if the home's last health inspection was more than two years ago, N if not.
cols.WITH_A_RESIDENT_AND_FAMILY_COUNCIL: Which kind of council the home has, like Resident or Both. Blank for about 6% of homes.
cols.NUMBER_OF_CERTIFIED_BEDS: How many beds the nursing home is certified to fill.
cols.AVERAGE_NUMBER_OF_RESIDENTS_PER_DAY: How many residents the home had on an average day, with a decimal.
cols.CHAIN_NAME: The nursing-home chain that owns or runs the home. Some chains are named after a person, like BENJAMIN LANDA.
cols.CHAIN_ID: CMS's ID number for the nursing-home chain. Blank when the home is not in a chain.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FACILITIES_IN_CHAIN: How many nursing homes are in the chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_OVERALL_5_STAR_RATING: The average overall star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The average inspection star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_STAFFING_RATING: The average staffing star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_QM_RATING: The average quality-of-care star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.OVERALL_RATING: The home's overall star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The home's inspection star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.STAFFING_RATING: The home's staffing star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.REPORTED_NURSE_AIDE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_R: Nurse aide hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them. 2.5 means two and a half hours.
cols.REPORTED_LPN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT: Licensed practical nurse hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_RN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_: Registered nurse hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_LICENSED_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RES: Hours per resident per day from licensed nurses, registered and practical combined, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_: All nursing hours per resident per day, aides and licensed nurses together, as the home reported them.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_NURSE_STAFF_HOURS_PER_RE: All nursing hours per resident per day on weekends only. Usually lower than the weekday number.
cols.REGISTERED_NURSE_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_PER_: Registered nurse hours per resident per day on weekends only.
cols.REPORTED_PHYSICAL_THERAPIST_STAFFING_HOU: Physical therapist hours per resident per day, as the home reported them. Usually a small fraction of an hour.
cols.NURSING_CASE_MIX_INDEX: A score for how much nursing care the home's residents need. Higher means sicker, needier residents.
cols.NURSING_CASE_MIX_INDEX_RATIO: The home's care-needs score divided by the national average. Above 1 means needier residents than average.
cols.TOTAL_NURSING_STAFF_TURNOVER: The percent of nursing staff who left over a year, from 0 to 100.
cols.REGISTERED_NURSE_TURNOVER: The percent of registered nurses who left over a year, from 0 to 100.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ADMINISTRATORS_WHO_HAVE_LEFT_T: How many administrators, the person running the home, left during the period CMS counts.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_STANDARD_SURVEY_HEALTH_DA: The date of the home's most recent routine health inspection. One table stores it as a date, the other as a date with a midnight time.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_DE: How many problems inspectors cited in the most recent inspection cycle, routine and complaint visits together.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_STANDARD_HEALTH: How many problems the most recent routine inspection cited.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_COMPLAINT_HEALT: How many problems were cited from complaint visits in the most recent inspection cycle.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_REVISITS: How many times inspectors had to come back to check fixes in the most recent inspection cycle.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_STANDARD_HEALTH_SURVEY_DA: The date of the home's second most recent routine health inspection. One table stores it as a date, the other as a date with a midnight time.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_: How many problems inspectors cited in the two earlier inspection cycles, routine and complaint visits together.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_NUMBER_OF_STANDARD_HEALTH: How many problems the second most recent routine inspection cited.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_NUMBER_OF_COMPLAINT_HEA: How many problems were cited from complaint visits in the two earlier inspection cycles.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_REVISI: How many times inspectors came back to check fixes in the two earlier inspection cycles.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FINES: How many fines the home was hit with in the period CMS counts.
cols.TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_FINES_IN_DOLLARS: The total of those fines, in dollars. Zero when there were none.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PAYMENT_DENIALS: How many times Medicare refused to pay the home for new admissions as a penalty.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_PENALTIES: Fines plus payment denials, added together.

cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A random ID for the load run that brought this row in. Some tables give every row its own ID, so do not group by it. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.SURVEY_DATE: The date of the inspection that found this problem.
cols.SURVEY_TYPE: What kind of inspection it was. Always Health in the health table and Fire Safety in the fire table.
cols.DEFICIENCY_PREFIX: The letter in front of the rule number: F for health rules, K or E for fire and emergency rules.
cols.DEFICIENCY_CATEGORY: The broad group the broken rule falls in, like Pharmacy Service Deficiencies or Smoke Deficiencies.
cols.DEFICIENCY_TAG_NUMBER: The four-digit number of the rule that was broken, kept as text so leading zeros stay. Put the prefix letter in front to get the full tag, like F0725.
cols.DEFICIENCY_DESCRIPTION: The rule that was broken, in plain words, like Provide enough nursing staff every day.
cols.SCOPE_SEVERITY_CODE: One letter from A to L grading how serious and how widespread the problem was. Later letters are worse.
cols.DEFICIENCY_CORRECTED: Where the fix stands, like has a date of correction, has a plan of correction, Past Non-Compliance, or waiver granted.
cols.CORRECTION_DATE: The date the home fixed or promised to fix the problem.
cols.INSPECTION_CYCLE: Which inspection round the finding came from: 1 is the most recent, then 2, then 3. Stored as text.
cols.STANDARD_DEFICIENCY: Y if the problem was found on a routine inspection, N if not. Always Y in the fire table.
cols.COMPLAINT_DEFICIENCY: Y if the problem was found on a visit sparked by a complaint, N if not. Always N in the fire table.
cols.INFECTION_CONTROL_INSPECTION_DEFICIENCY: Y if the problem was found on an infection-control inspection, N if not. Always N in the fire table.
cols.CITATION_UNDER_IDR: Y if the home is disputing this citation through the informal appeal process, N if not. Every sampled row is N.
cols.CITATION_UNDER_IIDR: Y if the citation is under the independent appeal process, N if not. Every sampled row is N.
cols.PROCESSING_DATE: The date CMS put out this batch of the file. The same date on every row of a table.

cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.MIDDLE_NAME: The person's middle name, or just an initial.
cols.BUSINESS_NAME: The name of the business, when the row is a business. Often blank because many rows are people.
cols.SPECIALTY: The provider's medical specialty or job, like Family Practice or Pharmacist.
cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit Medicare provider number, the National Provider Identifier. Stored as text.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion.

cols.HPSA_ID: The ID of a federally named doctor-shortage area, ten characters, sometimes ending in a letter. Stored as text.
cols.BHCMIS_ORGANIZATION_ID: The federal ID for a community health center organization, as text with leading zeros. Mostly blank in the shortage-area table.
cols.HPSA_NAME: The name of the doctor-shortage area, like a county, a neighborhood, a low-income group, or a clinic.
cols.HPSA_DISCIPLINE_CLASS: Which kind of care is short. Always Primary Care in these tables.
cols.DISCIPLINE_CLASS_NUMBER: A number for which kind of care is short. Always 1, meaning primary care. A number in one table, text in the other.
cols.HPSA_SCORE: How severe the doctor shortage is, 0 to 25. Higher means worse. Stored as text in one table.
cols.PC_MCTA_SCORE: A score for how short the area is on maternity care. Mostly blank, and stored as text with stray leading spaces in one table.
cols.HPSA_STATUS: Where the shortage designation stands: Designated, Proposed For Withdrawal, or Withdrawn.
cols.HPSA_STATUS_CODE: The same status as one letter: D Designated, P Proposed For Withdrawal, W Withdrawn.
cols.HPSA_TYPE_CODE: What kind of shortage area it is, like Hpsa Geo for a place, Hpsa Pop for a group of people, or a facility type like FQHC or ITU. Needs a lookup.
cols.WITHDRAWN_DATE: The date the shortage designation was withdrawn. Blank if still active. A real date in one table, month/day/year text in the other.
cols.BREAK_IN_DESIGNATION: Y if the shortage designation had a gap in time, N if not. Every sampled row is N.
cols.HPSA_FTE: How many full-time doctors the area has, counted in full-time equivalents, so 0.5 is one half-time doctor. Stored as text in one table.
cols.HPSA_SHORTAGE: How many more full-time doctors the area needs to end the shortage. Stored as text in one table, often blank.
cols.METROPOLITAN_INDICATOR: Whether the area is Metropolitan, Non-Metropolitan, Frontier, or Unknown.
cols.RURAL_STATUS: Whether the area or practice is rural. One table uses True or False; the others use Rural, Non-Rural, Partially Rural or Unknown.
cols.RURAL_STATUS_CODE: A one-letter rural code: R rural, N not rural, P partly rural, U unknown. Sometimes blank.
cols.US_MEXICO_BORDER_100KM_INDICATOR: Y if the place is within 100 kilometers of the Mexico border, N if not, U if unknown.
cols.US_MEXICO_BORDER_COUNTY_INDICATOR: Y if the place is in a county on the Mexico border, N if not, U if unknown.
cols.HPSA_ADDRESS: The street address of the shortage area, only when it is a single facility. Blank for about 90% of rows.
cols.HPSA_CITY: The city of the shortage area, only when it is a single facility. Blank for about 90% of rows.
cols.HPSA_POSTAL_CODE: The zip code of the shortage area, only when it is a single facility. Blank for about 90% of rows, sometimes with the four-digit add-on.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, in decimal degrees. U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.PRIMARY_STATE_ABBREVIATION: The area's state or territory, as two letters. Includes places like GU for Guam and MH for the Marshall Islands.
cols.PRIMARY_STATE_NAME: The area's state or territory, spelled out.
cols.PRIMARY_STATE_FIPS_CODE: The area's state as a two-digit federal code, kept as text with leading zeros.
cols.STATE_ABBREVIATION: The state as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam and AS for American Samoa appear too.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.STATE_FIPS_CODE: The state as a 2-digit Census code, like 06 for California. Territories use codes 60 and up.
cols.COMMON_STATE_ABBREVIATION: The area's state or territory, as two letters. Same values as the primary state column in these samples.
cols.COMMON_STATE_NAME: The area's state or territory, spelled out.
cols.COMMON_STATE_FIPS_CODE: The area's state as a two-digit federal code, kept as text with leading zeros.
cols.COMMON_COUNTY_NAME: The county with its state tacked on, like Polk County, FL.
cols.COMMON_STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE: The county as a five-digit federal code, state plus county, kept as text with leading zeros.
cols.COMMON_POSTAL_CODE: The five-digit zip code of the shortage area. Blank for about 90% of rows.
cols.COMMON_REGION_NAME: The federal health department region, like Region 4.
cols.COUNTY_EQUIVALENT_NAME: The county name, or the local equivalent in territories, like Rongelap in the Marshall Islands.
cols.STATE_COUNTY_FIPS_CODE: The county's five-digit government code, where the first two digits are the state. Kept as text so leading zeros survive.
cols.RECORD_CREATE_DATE: The date the source built the file. The same date, 2026-08-07, on every sampled row, so it says nothing about the individual record.

cols.CMS_CERTIFICATION_NUMBER_CCN: The nursing home's six-digit Medicare ID. Kept as text so leading zeros like 015073 survive.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.COUNTY_PARISH: The county name, or parish in Louisiana. Casing varies.
cols.OWNERSHIP_TYPE: Who owns it: for-profit, non-profit, government, cooperative, and so on. Wording differs by table.
cols.NUMBER_OF_CERTIFIED_BEDS: How many beds the nursing home is certified to fill.
cols.AVERAGE_NUMBER_OF_RESIDENTS_PER_DAY: How many residents the home had on an average day, with a decimal.
cols.PROVIDER_RESIDES_IN_HOSPITAL: Whether the nursing home is inside a hospital, Y or N.
cols.DATE_FIRST_APPROVED_TO_PROVIDE_MEDICARE_: The date the nursing home was first approved to take Medicare and Medicaid patients.
cols.CHAIN_NAME: The nursing-home chain that owns or runs the home. Some chains are named after a person, like BENJAMIN LANDA.
cols.CHAIN_ID: CMS's ID number for the nursing-home chain. Blank when the home is not in a chain.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FACILITIES_IN_CHAIN: How many nursing homes are in the chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_OVERALL_5_STAR_RATING: The average overall star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The average inspection star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_STAFFING_RATING: The average staffing star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CHAIN_AVERAGE_QM_RATING: The average quality-of-care star rating, 1 to 5, across all homes in the same chain. Blank when the home is not part of a chain.
cols.CONTINUING_CARE_RETIREMENT_COMMUNITY: Whether the nursing home is part of a retirement community with several levels of care, Y or N.
cols.SPECIAL_FOCUS_STATUS: Whether CMS put the nursing home on its watch list for homes with a record of serious problems: SFF means on it, SFF Candidate means in line for it. Blank for about 96% of homes.
cols.ABUSE_ICON: Y if the nursing home is marked with CMS's abuse warning icon, N if not.
cols.MOST_RECENT_HEALTH_INSPECTION_MORE_THAN_: Y if the home's last health inspection was more than two years ago, N if not.
cols.WITH_A_RESIDENT_AND_FAMILY_COUNCIL: Which kind of council the home has, like Resident or Both. Blank for about 6% of homes.
cols.OVERALL_RATING: The home's overall star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.HEALTH_INSPECTION_RATING: The home's inspection star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.STAFFING_RATING: The home's staffing star rating from CMS, 1 to 5 stars. 5 is best.
cols.REPORTED_NURSE_AIDE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_R: Nurse aide hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them. 2.5 means two and a half hours.
cols.REPORTED_LPN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT: Licensed practical nurse hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_RN_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_: Registered nurse hours worked per resident per day, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_LICENSED_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_RES: Hours per resident per day from licensed nurses, registered and practical combined, as the home reported them.
cols.REPORTED_TOTAL_NURSE_STAFFING_HOURS_PER_: All nursing hours per resident per day, aides and licensed nurses together, as the home reported them.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_NURSE_STAFF_HOURS_PER_RE: All nursing hours per resident per day on weekends only. Usually lower than the weekday number.
cols.REGISTERED_NURSE_HOURS_PER_RESIDENT_PER_: Registered nurse hours per resident per day on weekends only.
cols.REPORTED_PHYSICAL_THERAPIST_STAFFING_HOU: Physical therapist hours per resident per day, as the home reported them. Usually a small fraction of an hour.
cols.TOTAL_NURSING_STAFF_TURNOVER: The percent of nursing staff who left over a year, from 0 to 100.
cols.REGISTERED_NURSE_TURNOVER: The percent of registered nurses who left over a year, from 0 to 100.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ADMINISTRATORS_WHO_HAVE_LEFT_T: How many administrators, the person running the home, left during the period CMS counts.
cols.NURSING_CASE_MIX_INDEX: A score for how much nursing care the home's residents need. Higher means sicker, needier residents.
cols.NURSING_CASE_MIX_INDEX_RATIO: The home's care-needs score divided by the national average. Above 1 means needier residents than average.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_STANDARD_SURVEY_HEALTH_DA: The date of the home's most recent routine health inspection. One table stores it as a date, the other as a date with a midnight time.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_DE: How many problems inspectors cited in the most recent inspection cycle, routine and complaint visits together.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_STANDARD_HEALTH: How many problems the most recent routine inspection cited.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_COMPLAINT_HEALT: How many problems were cited from complaint visits in the most recent inspection cycle.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_1_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_REVISITS: How many times inspectors had to come back to check fixes in the most recent inspection cycle.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_STANDARD_HEALTH_SURVEY_DA: The date of the home's second most recent routine health inspection. One table stores it as a date, the other as a date with a midnight time.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_: How many problems inspectors cited in the two earlier inspection cycles, routine and complaint visits together.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_NUMBER_OF_STANDARD_HEALTH: How many problems the second most recent routine inspection cited.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_NUMBER_OF_COMPLAINT_HEA: How many problems were cited from complaint visits in the two earlier inspection cycles.
cols.RATING_CYCLE_2_3_NUMBER_OF_HEALTH_REVISI: How many times inspectors came back to check fixes in the two earlier inspection cycles.
cols.NUMBER_OF_FINES: How many fines the home was hit with in the period CMS counts.
cols.TOTAL_AMOUNT_OF_FINES_IN_DOLLARS: The total of those fines, in dollars. Zero when there were none.
cols.NUMBER_OF_PAYMENT_DENIALS: How many times Medicare refused to pay the home for new admissions as a penalty.
cols.TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_PENALTIES: Fines plus payment denials, added together.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.

cols.ARRPORT: The first port the ship meant to land at, as a five-digit place code. Often blank.

cols.BOYRAT7: Share of the captives who were boys, as a decimal from 0 to 1, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.CAPTAINA: The name of the ship's first captain, last name first. Accented letters sometimes show as a broken character.
cols.CAPTAINB: The name of the ship's second captain, last name first. Mostly blank.
cols.CHIL1IMP: The estimated number of children put aboard, worked out by the editors. Almost always blank.
cols.CHIL3IMP: Estimated number of enslaved children on the voyage, filled in by the source where the record was incomplete, at the source's third counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.

cols.CHILD3: How many children, sex not given, were landed at the first landing place. Almost always blank.

cols.CREW3: How many crew were aboard at another stage of the voyage. Mostly blank.
cols.DATEDEPA: The day of the month the voyage started. Pair with the month and year columns. Often blank.
cols.DATEDEPB: The month the voyage started, 1 to 12. Often blank.
cols.DATEDEPC: The year the voyage started. Often blank.
cols.D1SLATRA: The day of the month the buying of enslaved people began. Almost always blank.
cols.D1SLATRB: The month the buying of enslaved people began. Almost always blank.
cols.D1SLATRC: The year the buying of enslaved people began. Almost always blank.
cols.DLSLATRA: The day of the month the ship left the last place it bought enslaved people. Mostly blank.
cols.DLSLATRB: The month the ship left the last place it bought enslaved people. Mostly blank.
cols.DLSLATRC: The year the ship left the last place it bought enslaved people. Mostly blank.

cols.DATARR33: The month enslaved people were first landed, 1 to 12.
cols.DATARR34: The year enslaved people were first landed.
cols.DATARR36: The day of the month for a later arrival in the voyage. Almost always blank.
cols.DATARR37: The month for a later arrival in the voyage. Almost always blank.
cols.DATARR38: The year for a later arrival in the voyage. Almost always blank.
cols.DATARR39: The day of the month for a late stage of the voyage.
cols.DATARR40: The month for a late stage of the voyage. Almost always empty.
cols.DATARR41: The year for a late stage of the voyage. Almost always empty.
cols.FATE: How the voyage ended, as a number code. Needs the database codebook.
cols.FATE2: What happened to the enslaved people on board, as a number code. Needs the database codebook.
cols.FATE3: What happened to the ship if it was captured or lost, as a number code. Needs the database codebook.
cols.FATE4: How the voyage turned out for the owners, as a number code from 1 to 3. Needs the database codebook.
cols.FEMALE1: How many females, age not given, were put aboard at the first buying place. Almost always blank.

cols.FEML3IMP: Estimated number of enslaved females on the voyage, filled in by the source where the record was incomplete, at the source's third counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.

cols.GIRL3: How many girls were landed at the first landing place. Mostly blank.
cols.GIRL7: How many enslaved girls were counted on the voyage, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.

cols.INFANT1: How many infants were put aboard at the first buying place. Almost always blank.

cols.MAJBUYPT: The main place enslaved people were bought, as a five-digit place code.
cols.MAJBYIMP: The main region enslaved people were bought in, as a place code ending in 00, filled in by the editors where missing.

cols.MAJSELPT: The main place enslaved people were landed, as a five-digit place code.

cols.MALRAT7: Share of the captives who were males, as a decimal from 0 to 1, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.MEN1: How many men were put aboard at the first buying place. Almost always blank.
cols.MEN3: How many men were landed at the first landing place. Mostly blank.
cols.MEN7: How many enslaved men were counted on the voyage, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.MENRAT7: Share of the captives who were men, as a decimal from 0 to 1, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.

cols.MJSELIMP: The main region enslaved people were landed in, as a place code ending in 00, filled in by the editors where missing.

cols.OWNERB: The name of the ship's second listed owner. Mostly blank, and some entries are just a dot.

cols.OWNERD: The name of the ship's fourth listed owner. Mostly blank.
cols.OWNERE: The name of the ship's fifth listed owner. Almost always blank.
cols.OWNERF: The name of the ship's sixth listed owner. Almost always blank.

cols.PLACCONS: Where the ship was built, as a five-digit place code. Mostly blank.
cols.PLACREG: Where the ship was registered, as a five-digit place code. Mostly blank.

cols.REGDIS1: The region where enslaved people were first landed, as a place code ending in 00.
cols.REGDIS2: The region of the second landing place, as a place code ending in 00. Almost always blank.

cols.REGEM2: The region of the second buying place, as a place code ending in 00. Almost always blank.
cols.REGISREG: The region where the ship was registered, as a place code ending in 00. Mostly blank.

cols.RIG: A number code for the ship's rig type, the way its sails are set up. Needs the database codebook.
cols.SHIPNAME: The ship's name. Accented letters sometimes show as a broken character.
cols.SLA1PORT: The first place enslaved people were landed, as a five-digit place code.
cols.SLAARRIV: How many enslaved people were still alive when the ship arrived. Stored as text.
cols.SLADAMER: A count of enslaved people tied to landing in the Americas. Almost always blank.
cols.SLADVOY: How many enslaved people died during the voyage, as recorded. Often blank.
cols.SLAMIMP: The estimated number of enslaved people landed alive. Filled on every row. Stored as text.
cols.SLAS32: How many enslaved people were landed at the first landing place, as recorded. Mostly blank.
cols.SLAS36: How many enslaved people were landed at the second landing place, as recorded. Almost always blank.
cols.SLAS39: How many enslaved people were landed at the third landing place, as recorded. Almost always blank.

cols.SLAVEMA3: How many captives had their age recorded, at the source's third counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.SLAVEMA7: How many captives had their age recorded, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.SLAVEMX1: How many of those put aboard had their sex recorded. Almost always blank.
cols.SLAVEMX3: How many captives had their sex recorded, at the source's third counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.SLAVEMX7: How many captives had their sex recorded, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.

cols.SLAVMAX3: How many captives had both age and sex recorded, at the source's third counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.SLAVMAX7: How many captives had both age and sex recorded, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.SLAXIMP: The estimated number of enslaved people put aboard. Filled on every row, unlike the recorded count. Stored as text.
cols.SOURCEA: The first source the voyage record rests on, as a short archive or book citation.
cols.SOURCEB: The second source citation for the voyage record. Often blank.
cols.SOURCEC: The third source citation for the voyage record. Often blank.
cols.SOURCED: The fourth source citation for the voyage record. Often blank.
cols.SOURCEE: The fifth source citation for the voyage record. Often blank.
cols.TONNAGE: The ship's size in tons. Mostly blank.
cols.TSLAVESD: How many enslaved people were put aboard, as recorded in the sources. Often blank. Stored as text.
cols.TSLMTIMP: The estimated number put aboard, used by the editors to work out the death rate. Often blank.
cols.VOY2IMP: How many days the crossing took, estimated by the database's editors. Often blank.
cols.VOYAGE: How many days the crossing took, as recorded. Mostly blank.
cols.VYMRTIMP: How many enslaved people died during the voyage, estimated by the database's editors. Often blank.
cols.VYMRTRAT: The share of enslaved people who died on the voyage, as a fraction, so 0.28 means 28%. Stored as text.
cols.WOMEN1: How many women were put aboard at the first buying place. Almost always blank.
cols.WOMEN3: How many women were landed at the first landing place. Mostly blank.
cols.WOMEN7: How many enslaved women were counted on the voyage, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.WOMRAT7: Share of the captives who were women, as a decimal from 0 to 1, at the source's seventh counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.YEAR10: Which ten-year period the voyage falls in, as a bucket number like 33, not a calendar year.
cols.YEAR100: The century the voyage falls in, as its first year like 1700.
cols.YEAR25: Which 25-year period the voyage falls in, as a bucket number like 13, not a calendar year.
cols.YEAR5: Which five-year period the voyage falls in, as a bucket number like 64, not a calendar year.
cols.YEARAM: The year the ship arrived to land the captives, like 1817.
cols.YRCONS: The year the ship was built. Mostly blank.
cols.YRREG: The year the ship was registered. Blank in the transatlantic table.
cols.VOYAGEID2: The ID of a second, linked voyage. Almost always blank, and some values are padded with leading spaces.
cols.INTRAAMER: 1 if the voyage stayed inside the Americas, 0 if it crossed the Atlantic from Africa. The same value on every row of each table.
cols.BOYRAT1: The share of those put aboard who were boys, as a fraction. Almost always blank.
cols.CHILRAT1: The share of those put aboard who were children, as a fraction. Almost always blank.
cols.GIRLRAT1: The share of those put aboard who were girls, as a fraction. Almost always blank.
cols.MALRAT1: The share of those put aboard who were male, as a fraction. Almost always blank.
cols.MENRAT1: The share of those put aboard who were men, as a fraction, so 0.35 means 35%. Almost always blank.
cols.WOMRAT1: The share of those put aboard who were women, as a fraction. Almost always blank.
cols.BOYRAT3: Share of the captives who were boys, as a decimal from 0 to 1, at the source's third counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.CHILRAT3: Share of the captives who were children, as a decimal from 0 to 1, at the source's third counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.
cols.GIRLRAT3: Share of the captives who were girls, as a decimal from 0 to 1, at the source's third counting stage; the SlaveVoyages codebook says which stage that is. Stored as text and mostly blank.

cols.PERSON_NAME: The name of the person tied to the record. Some tables mix in company names or court case names.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's two-digit number code, like 06 for California. One table drops the leading zero, so 1 means 01.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.DOCUMENT_TYPE: What kind of document it is, like SEC insider Form 4 or a FARA Supplemental Statement. Categories depend on the source.
cols.SUBJECTS: Subject tags for the item, several in one field split by | or ;.
cols.FULL_TEXT: Meant to hold the document's full text, but in the WPA table it holds catalog descriptions like 1 photographic print.
cols.SOURCE_ID: A short internal name for the source feed the row came from, like fed_cfpb_complaints.
cols._INGESTED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse, as a date and time. Added by your pipeline, not the source.
cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A random ID for the load run that brought this row in. Some tables give every row its own ID, so do not group by it. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.ACTIVITY_YEAR: The year of the mortgage data, like 2022.
cols.LEI: The company's Legal Entity Identifier, a 20-character global ID. The FDIC table's values are only 16 characters, so they look cut short.
cols.DERIVED_MSA_MD: The metro area code for the property, 5 digits like 47894 for the Washington DC area. 99999 means not in a metro area.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state. Usually two letters like TX, but the EPA air-monitor table uses the two-digit number code, like 01 for Alabama.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code. Written different ways: three digits like 001, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like LA099.
cols.CENSUS_TRACT: The census tract, a neighborhood-sized area. Mortgage tables give the full 11-digit code with state and county first; the HUD table gives only the 6-digit tract part.
cols.CONFORMING_LOAN_LIMIT: C if the loan is under the size limit for standard government-backed mortgages, NC if it is over.
cols.DERIVED_LOAN_PRODUCT_TYPE: The loan type and lien position together, like FHA:First Lien.
cols.DERIVED_DWELLING_CATEGORY: The kind of home, like Single Family 1-4 Units:Site-Built or Multifamily.
cols.DERIVED_ETHNICITY: The borrowers' ethnicity as summed up by the CFPB: Hispanic or Latino, Not Hispanic or Latino, Joint, or Not Available.
cols.DERIVED_RACE: The borrowers' race as summed up by the CFPB, like White, Asian, Joint or Race Not Available.
cols.DERIVED_SEX: The borrowers' sex as summed up by the CFPB: Male, Female, Joint or Sex Not Available.
cols.ACTION_TAKEN: What the lender did with the mortgage application, as a number code: 1 means the loan was made; others like denied or withdrawn need a lookup.
cols.PURCHASER_TYPE: Who bought the mortgage from the lender, as a number code. 0 means it was not sold; others like Fannie Mae need a lookup.
cols.PREAPPROVAL: Whether the borrower asked for preapproval: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.LOAN_TYPE: The kind of mortgage: 1 regular, 2 FHA, 3 VA, 4 USDA rural.
cols.LOAN_PURPOSE: What the mortgage was for. HMDA tables use number codes like 1 for buying a home that need a lookup; the HUD table says it in words like Purchase.
cols.LIEN_STATUS: Where the loan stands in line to be paid back if the home is sold: 1 first, 2 second. The historic table adds 3 and 4, which need a lookup.
cols.REVERSE_MORTGAGE: 1 if it is a reverse mortgage, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt from reporting it.
cols.OPEN_END_LINE_OF_CREDIT: 1 if it is an open-ended credit line like a home equity line, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt.
cols.BUSINESS_OR_COMMERCIAL_PURPOSE: 1 if the loan is mainly for business, 2 if not, 1111 if the lender is exempt.
cols.LOAN_AMOUNT: The loan amount in dollars, rounded to the middle of a $10,000 band, so 515000 covers 510,000 to 519,999.
cols.LOAN_TO_VALUE_RATIO: The loan as a percent of the property's value, like 95.0. Stored as text in two tables; values like 999.999 are suspect.
cols.INTEREST_RATE: The mortgage interest rate, as a percent like 6.125. Blank for loans not made, and stored as text in some tables.
cols.RATE_SPREAD: How many percentage points the loan's rate sits above the typical rate for a prime borrower. Can be negative, mostly blank, and stored as text in some tables.
cols.HOEPA_STATUS: Whether it was a high-cost loan under federal rules: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.TOTAL_LOAN_COSTS: Total closing costs the borrower paid, in dollars. Stored as text in two tables and often blank.
cols.TOTAL_POINTS_AND_FEES: Total points and fees on the loan, in dollars. Almost always blank; some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.ORIGINATION_CHARGES: The lender's fees for making the loan, in dollars. Stored as text in two tables and often blank.
cols.DISCOUNT_POINTS: Dollars the borrower paid up front to get a lower interest rate. Stored as text in two tables and often blank.
cols.LENDER_CREDITS: Dollars the lender paid toward the borrower's closing costs. Mostly blank; stored as text in some tables, where it can read Exempt.
cols.LOAN_TERM: How long the loan runs, in months, like 360 for 30 years. Stored as text; some rows say Exempt instead of a number.
cols.PREPAYMENT_PENALTY_TERM: How many months the loan charges a penalty for paying it off early, like 36. Mostly blank; can read Exempt in the text versions.
cols.INTRO_RATE_PERIOD: How many months the loan's starting teaser rate lasts before it can change, like 60 or 84. Blank for fixed-rate loans; can read Exempt.
cols.NEGATIVE_AMORTIZATION: Whether the loan balance can grow even when you pay: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.INTEREST_ONLY_PAYMENT: Whether the loan lets you pay only interest for a while: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.BALLOON_PAYMENT: Whether the loan ends with one big lump payment: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt from reporting.
cols.OTHER_NONAMORTIZING_FEATURES: Whether the loan has some other feature that keeps the balance from paying down normally: 1 yes, 2 no, 1111 exempt.
cols.PROPERTY_VALUE: The home's value in dollars, rounded to the middle of a 10,000 band, so values end in 5000. Stored as text in some tables.
cols.CONSTRUCTION_METHOD: How the home was built, as a code: 1 site-built, 2 manufactured home.
cols.OCCUPANCY_TYPE: How the borrower will use the home, as a code: 1 main home, 2 second home, 3 rental or investment.
cols.MANUFACTURED_HOME_SECURED_PROPERTY_TYPE: For manufactured homes, whether the loan covers the home and land or just the home, as a code. 3 means not a manufactured home; 1111 means exempt.
cols.MANUFACTURED_HOME_LAND_PROPERTY_INTEREST: For manufactured homes, whether the borrower owns or leases the land underneath, as a code. 5 means not a manufactured home; 1111 means exempt.
cols.TOTAL_UNITS: How many homes or apartments are in the property. The mortgage tables store it as text with ranges like 5-24.
cols.MULTIFAMILY_AFFORDABLE_UNITS: For apartment buildings, how many units are income-restricted affordable housing. Almost always blank; can read Exempt in the text versions.
cols.DEBT_TO_INCOME_RATIO: The borrower's monthly debt as a share of income. Mixes bands like 30%-<36% with exact numbers like 41, plus Exempt, so it is text, not a number.
cols.APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE: Which credit scoring model the lender used for the borrower, as a number code like 1 or 3; 9 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE: Which credit scoring model the lender used for the co-borrower, as a number code; 10 means no co-borrower, 9 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code like 1 Hispanic or 2 not Hispanic, with subgroups like 11 to 14. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The co-borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code; 5 means no co-borrower. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The co-borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The co-borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The co-borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The co-borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_1: The borrower's first listed race, as a number code like 5 for White or 3 for Black. Two-digit codes are subgroups; needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_2: The borrower's second listed race, as a number code like 5 for White. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_3: The borrower's third listed race, as a number code. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_4: The borrower's fourth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_5: The borrower's fifth listed race, as a number code. Every sampled row is blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_1: The co-applicant's race as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup, like 5 for White or 3 for Black. 8 means there is no co-applicant.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_2: A second race the co-applicant picked, as a number code like 22 or 5. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_3: A third race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_4: A fourth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_5: A fifth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.

cols.MANUFACTURED_HOME_LAND_PROPERTY_INTEREST: For manufactured homes, whether the borrower owns or leases the land underneath, as a code. 5 means not a manufactured home; 1111 means exempt.
cols.TOTAL_UNITS: How many homes or apartments are in the property. The mortgage tables store it as text with ranges like 5-24.
cols.MULTIFAMILY_AFFORDABLE_UNITS: For apartment buildings, how many units are income-restricted affordable housing. Almost always blank; can read Exempt in the text versions.
cols.DEBT_TO_INCOME_RATIO: The borrower's monthly debt as a share of income. Mixes bands like 30%-<36% with exact numbers like 41, plus Exempt, so it is text, not a number.
cols.APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE: Which credit scoring model the lender used for the borrower, as a number code like 1 or 3; 9 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_CREDIT_SCORE_TYPE: Which credit scoring model the lender used for the co-borrower, as a number code; 10 means no co-borrower, 9 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code like 1 Hispanic or 2 not Hispanic, with subgroups like 11 to 14. Needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_1: The co-borrower's first listed ethnicity, as a number code; 5 means no co-borrower. Needs a lookup.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_2: The co-borrower's second listed ethnicity, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_3: The co-borrower's third listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_4: The co-borrower's fourth listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_5: The co-borrower's fifth listed ethnicity, as a number code.
cols.APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_ETHNICITY_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's ethnicity by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_1: The borrower's first listed race, as a number code like 5 for White or 3 for Black. Two-digit codes are subgroups; needs a lookup.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_2: The borrower's second listed race, as a number code like 5 for White. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_3: The borrower's third listed race, as a number code. Blank for almost everyone.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_4: The borrower's fourth listed race, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_5: The borrower's fifth listed race, as a number code. Every sampled row is blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_1: The co-applicant's race as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup, like 5 for White or 3 for Black. 8 means there is no co-applicant.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_2: A second race the co-applicant picked, as a number code like 22 or 5. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_3: A third race the co-applicant picked, as a number code. Almost always blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_4: A fourth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_5: A fifth race the co-applicant picked, as a number code.
cols.APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_RACE_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's race by looks or surname: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX: The applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable. The newer file also uses 6 for picked both.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX: The co-applicant's sex as a number code: 1 male, 2 female, 3 not provided, 4 not applicable, 5 no co-applicant. The newer files also use 6 for picked both.
cols.APPLICANT_SEX_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the borrower's sex by looks or name: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_SEX_OBSERVED: Whether the lender guessed the co-borrower's sex by looks or name: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 4 no co-borrower.
cols.APPLICANT_AGE: The applicant's age as a range like 25-34, not an exact age. Bands differ by source, and 8888 means not applicable.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_AGE: The co-borrower's age band, like 25-34 or >74. 9999 means no co-borrower and 8888 means not applicable.
cols.APPLICANT_AGE_ABOVE_62: Whether the borrower is over 62, as Yes or No. Sometimes blank.
cols.CO_APPLICANT_AGE_ABOVE_62: Whether the co-borrower is over 62, as Yes or No. Mostly blank, since most loans have no co-borrower.
cols.SUBMISSION_OF_APPLICATION: Whether the borrower applied straight to this lender, as a code: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 1111 exempt.
cols.INITIALLY_PAYABLE_TO_INSTITUTION: Whether the loan was first owed to this lender, as a code: 1 yes, 2 no, 3 not applicable, 1111 exempt.
cols.AUS_1: The first automated underwriting system the lender ran the loan through, as a number code like 1 or 2; 6 not applicable, 1111 exempt. Needs a lookup.
cols.AUS_2: A second automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Mostly blank.
cols.AUS_3: A third automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.AUS_4: A fourth automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.AUS_5: A fifth automated underwriting system the lender used, as a number code. Nearly always blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_1: The main reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. 10 means not applicable and 1111 means the lender is exempt; the older file is blank unless denied.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_2: A second reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Mostly blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_3: A third reason the loan was turned down, as a number code that needs the HMDA lookup. Almost always blank.
cols.DENIAL_REASON_4: A fourth reason the loan was turned down, as a number code like 4 or 9. Nearly always blank. Needs a lookup.
cols.TRACT_POPULATION: How many people live in the home's census tract, the neighborhood-sized area the Census counts.
cols.TRACT_MINORITY_POPULATION_PERCENT: The share of the home's census tract that is minority, as a percent from 0 to 100.
cols.FFIEC_MSA_MD_MEDIAN_FAMILY_INCOME: The median family income in dollars for the home's metro area, the same for every loan in that area. 0 shows up where there is no metro area.
cols.TRACT_TO_MSA_INCOME_PERCENTAGE: The census tract's median family income as a percent of its metro area's, so 100 is average and 50 is half. 0 means missing.
cols.TRACT_OWNER_OCCUPIED_UNITS: How many homes in the census tract are lived in by their owners.
cols.TRACT_ONE_TO_FOUR_FAMILY_HOMES: How many houses in the census tract hold one to four families.
cols.TRACT_MEDIAN_AGE_OF_HOUSING_UNITS: The typical age in years of homes in the census tract. 0 likely means missing.

cols.NOTE: A free-text note about the record. Empty for most rows.

cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.COMPANY: The company the record is about, like the one a consumer complained about or the one that won a research award. Blank in most rows of the FHFA tables.
cols.CITY: The city or town name. Mostly in capitals, sometimes mixed case, and spellings are not cleaned.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.

cols.STATES: The state or states the record covers. A list of two-letter codes like MA,ME,NH in the watershed table, where CN means Canada; code plus name like AK Alaska in the HUD table.

cols.TOTAL_UNITS: How many homes or apartments are in the property. The mortgage tables store it as text with ranges like 5-24.
cols.TOTAL_OCCUPIED: How many subsidized units are occupied. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not counts.
cols.PCT_OCCUPIED: Percent of subsidized units that are occupied. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not percents.
cols.NUMBER_REPORTED: How many units sent in tenant reports to HUD. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not counts.
cols.PCT_REPORTED: Percent of units that sent in tenant reports to HUD. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not percents.
cols.SPENDING_PER_MONTH: Average HUD dollars spent per unit per month. Negative values like -4 are codes for missing or hidden data, not dollars.
cols.PCT_MINORITY: The percent of people nearby, or living in the housing project, who are minorities, like 33.7. The HUD table stores it as text and has bad values like -4.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, in decimal degrees. U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.PHA_TOTAL_UNITS: Total housing units run by the local public housing authority. Stored as text and often blank in the projects table.
cols.STD_CITY: The city of the address, cleaned up to a standard spelling.
cols.STD_ZIP5: The five-digit zip code of the address, stored as text so leading zeros stay.

cols.ENROLLMENT_ID: Medicare's ID for one enrollment record: the letter O, a date, then a number, like O20090204000452.
cols.ENROLLMENT_STATE: The state where the provider is enrolled in Medicare, as two letters.
cols.PROVIDER_TYPE_CODE: Medicare's code for the kind of provider, like 00-09 for a hospital. Each table mostly holds one value.
cols.PROVIDER_TYPE_TEXT: The kind of provider in words, like PART A PROVIDER - HOSPITAL.
cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit Medicare provider number, the National Provider Identifier. Stored as text.
cols.MULTIPLE_NPI_FLAG: Y if this enrollment covers more than one provider number, N if not.
cols.CCN: The facility's 6-character Medicare certification number. Stored as text; some hold letters, like 37T056.
cols.ASSOCIATE_ID: Medicare's 10-digit ID for the enrolled organization, used to link its enrollments and owners. Stored as text; a few look short, like lost leading zeros.
cols.ORGANIZATION_NAME: The name of the organization, like a charity, clinic, or home health agency.
cols.DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The name the facility operates under, when it differs from its legal name. Often empty.
cols.INCORPORATION_DATE: The date the company or organization was legally formed.
cols.INCORPORATION_STATE: The state where the organization is legally formed, as two letters. Often empty.
cols.ORGANIZATION_TYPE_STRUCTURE: The organization's legal form: CORPORATION, LLC, PARTNERSHIP, SOLE PROPRIETOR, or OTHER.

cols.PROPRIETARY_NONPROFIT: Whether the facility is for-profit or non-profit: P for for-profit, N for non-profit. Some tables also have D.

cols.EMPLOYER_NAME: The employer's name. In lobbying tables it is the client that hired the lobbyist; in donation tables it is the donor's employer.
cols.EMPLOYER_CITY: The city of the employer. Casing and naming vary, like Bronx versus The Bronx.
cols.EMPLOYER_STATE: The state of the employer, as two letters.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The six-digit industry code, like 722110 for restaurants. Needs a lookup to read; 000000 means not given.

cols.ENTRY_DATE: The date the person entered the U.S. Blank on most rows.

, and most court rows are blank.

cols.NAME_TYPE: Whether this row is the main name, a variation of it, or an alias. Capitalization is inconsistent, so "Primary name" and "Primary Name" both appear.
cols.ALIAS_STRENGTH: How solid an alias is: "Good quality a.k.a" or "Low quality a.k.a". Blank for main names.
cols.REGIME_NAME: The UK sanctions law the target is listed under, like The Syria Sanctions EU Exit Regulations.
cols.DESIGNATION_SOURCE: Who put the target on the list: UK, UN, or both as "UK|UN".
cols.SANCTIONS_IMPOSED: Which penalties apply, split by "|", like Asset freeze|Travel Ban.
cols.OTHER_INFORMATION: Free-text notes about the target, like which UN paragraph it was listed under or who runs it.
cols.UK_STATEMENT_OF_REASONS: The UK government's written reason for listing the target, in plain sentences. Some start with a stray space.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the street address, like 13 STATION ROAD.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second address line, usually a suite or floor. Often empty.
cols.ADDRESS_COUNTRY: The country of the address, spelled out, like Kenya or United Kingdom.
cols.ADDRESS_POSTAL_CODE: The postal code of the address, like BS8 3TU in the UK. Shapes vary by country, and it is mostly blank in the sanctions lists.
cols.DATE_DESIGNATED: The date the target was put on the UK sanctions list. Mostly blank in one of the two tables.
cols.LAST_UPDATED: The date the record was last updated at the source.
cols.NATIONALITIES: The country or countries the sanctioned person is a national of, like Syria or Russia. Often blank.
cols.PASSPORT_NUMBER: The target's passport number. Some start with a stray apostrophe or end with a hidden space, so clean before matching.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex. Written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses.
cols.TOWN_OF_BIRTH: The town or area where the sanctioned person was born.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_BIRTH: The country a person was born in, spelled out, like Kenya or Russia.
cols.TYPE_OF_ENTITY: What kind of business or group the target is, in free text, like Limited Liability Company or Research Institute. Mostly blank.
cols.SUBSIDIARIES: Companies the target owns or controls, by name. Mostly blank.
cols.PARENT_COMPANY: The company or body that owns this one. The greenhouse-gas table tacks on the ownership share, like 100%.
cols.IMO_NUMBER: The ship's 7-digit IMO number, a permanent international hull ID. Some tables put IMO in front of the digits, some do not.
cols.TYPE_OF_SHIP: What kind of ship a sanctioned vessel is, like Oil Tanker. Blank for anything that is not a ship.
cols.NON_LATIN_SCRIPT_TYPE: The alphabet the name is written in when not Latin letters, like Arabic, Cyrillic or Chinese. Mostly blank.
cols.NON_LATIN_SCRIPT_LANGUAGE: The language of the non-Latin version of the name, like Russian or Persian. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_3: The third line of the target's address, like a street or building. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_4: The fourth line of the target's address, like a district or P.O. box. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_5: The fifth line of the target's address, like a district or P.O. box. Mostly blank.
cols.ADDRESS_LINE_6: The sixth line of the target's address, usually the city or region.
cols.PHONE_NUMBER: A phone number, typed in mixed formats: with or without dashes, and with country codes for foreign numbers. Blank for many rows.
cols.WEBSITE: The organization's website address. Formats vary, with or without www or https.
cols.EMAIL_ADDRESS: An email address for the person, company or group. Fakes like no@email show up in the IRS 527 files.
cols.NATIONAL_IDENTIFIER_ADDITIONAL_INFORMATI: Notes about the target's national ID number, like which country or kind of card it is. Mostly blank.
cols.PASSPORT_ADDITIONAL_INFORMATION: Notes about the passport, like the issuing country or date.
cols.PREVIOUS_FLAGS: Countries a sanctioned ship used to sail under, like Panama. Almost always blank.
cols.TONNAGE_OF_SHIP: A sanctioned ship's tonnage, its size by cargo capacity. Stored as text, blank for non-ships.
cols.LENGTH_OF_SHIP: A sanctioned ship's length. Stored as text, no unit given, blank for non-ships.
cols.YEAR_BUILT: The year a sanctioned ship was built, like 2005. Stored as text, blank for non-ships.

cols._SOURCE_RUN_ID: A random ID for the load run that brought this row in. Some tables give every row its own ID, so do not group by it. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.REFERENCE_NUMBER: The source's reference number for the record, like QDi.150 on the UN sanctions list or R0004075 for a New York City donation.
cols.RECORD_TYPE: What kind of record this is: INDIVIDUAL or ENTITY on the UN sanctions list, always "registrations" in the study registrations table.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex. Written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses.
cols.NATIONALITY: The person's nationality. Format differs by table: words like British, two-letter codes like EG in immigration court, or wrapped like {"VALUE": "Yemen"} in the UN list.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. Some tables store it as text and a few use a range like 2000-2002.
cols.COUNTY_FIPS: The county's five-digit number code, like 01001. Stored as text so leading zeros survive.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some add the word county or municipio, so clean it before matching.
cols.STATE_ABBR: The state, as two letters like AL.
cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's two-digit number code, like 06 for California. One table drops the leading zero, so 1 means 01.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state. Usually two letters like TX, but the EPA air-monitor table uses the two-digit number code, like 01 for Alabama.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code. Written different ways: three digits like 001, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like LA099.
cols.URBANICITY: How built-up the county is: urban, suburban, small/mid or rural.
cols.TOTAL_JAIL_POP: How many people in total were held in the county jail.
cols.BLACK_JAIL_POP: How many Black people were held in the county jail. Whole numbers stored as text in one table, decimal estimates in the other.
cols.WHITE_JAIL_POP: How many white people were held in the county jail. Whole numbers stored as text in one table, decimal estimates in the other.

cols.SRC_SHA256: A fingerprint of the source file this row came from, used to spot changed files. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.AGE: The person's age in years, or an age group like 15-24 years in the CDC table. Stored as text in some tables.
cols.GENDER: The person's sex. Written differently by table: Male or Female, M or F, m or f, or Male Owned for businesses.
cols.RACE: The person's race as the source recorded it. Some tables spell it out like White or Asian, others use one-letter codes like W or B.
cols.CITY: The city or town name. Mostly in capitals, sometimes mixed case, and spellings are not cleaned.
cols.COUNTY: The county name, without the word County. Mostly U.S. counties, but the UK company table holds UK counties.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.LATITUDE: How far north the place is, in decimal degrees. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
cols.LONGITUDE: How far east or west the place is, in decimal degrees. U.S. places are negative. Some rows hold 0.0, which means no real location.
