cols.ESTABLISHMENT_NAME: The name of the business or work site, as the company wrote it. Some are just codes or branch numbers.
cols.ESTABLISHMENT_ID: OSHA's ID number for the work site. Use it to join the injury summary and case tables.
cols.EIN: The organization's 9-digit federal tax ID number, stored as text so leading zeros survive.

cols.CITY: The city or town name. Mostly in capitals, sometimes mixed case, and spellings are not cleaned.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.ZIP_CODE: The ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros survive. Some are 5 digits, some 9 with or without a dash.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The six-digit industry code, like 722110 for restaurants. Needs a lookup to read; 000000 means not given.
cols.NAICS_YEAR: Which edition of the industry code list was used: 2012, 2017, or 2022. Some tables add .0, and 0 means not given.
cols.INDUSTRY_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, as the employer wrote it. Not standardized, so the same industry is spelled several ways.
cols.SIZE: A code for how many people work at the site, like 1, 2, 3, 21, or 22. Needs OSHA's lookup to read.
cols.ANNUAL_AVERAGE_EMPLOYEES: The average number of employees at the site over the year. Some tables add .0.
cols.TOTAL_HOURS_WORKED: The total hours all employees worked at the site that year. Stored as text in two tables.
cols.NO_INJURIES_ILLNESSES: Whether the workplace had any injuries or illnesses that year, as a 1 or 2 code. Check OSHA's key for which is which; text in the 2025 table.
cols.TOTAL_DEATHS: How many workers died from work injuries or illnesses at this workplace that year.
cols.TOTAL_DAFW_CASES: How many injury or illness cases kept a worker home from work at this workplace that year. Shows decimals like 9.0 in the 2025 table.
cols.TOTAL_DJTR_CASES: How many cases moved a worker to another job or light duty instead of sending them home, that year. Shows decimals in the 2025 table.
cols.TOTAL_OTHER_CASES: How many recordable cases needed neither time off nor light duty, that year. Shows decimals in the 2025 table.
cols.TOTAL_DAFW_DAYS: Total days workers spent home from work because of injuries or illnesses at this workplace that year.
cols.TOTAL_DJTR_DAYS: Total days workers spent on light duty or moved to another job because of injuries or illnesses, that year.
cols.TOTAL_SKIN_DISORDERS: How many work-related skin illnesses, like rashes or burns from chemicals, this workplace recorded that year.
cols.TOTAL_RESPIRATORY_CONDITIONS: How many work-related breathing illnesses this workplace recorded that year.
cols.TOTAL_POISONINGS: How many work-related poisonings this workplace recorded that year. Almost always 0.
cols.TOTAL_HEARING_LOSS: How many cases of work-related hearing loss this workplace recorded that year.
cols.TOTAL_OTHER_ILLNESSES: How many other work-related illnesses, not skin, breathing, poisoning or hearing, this workplace recorded that year.
cols.CREATED_TIMESTAMP: When the report was sent to OSHA. Watch out: two tables show year 0024 or 0026 when they mean 2024 or 2026.
cols.CHANGE_REASON: The employer's own note on why they changed or resubmitted their yearly report, typed freely. Mostly blank; junk like 0 and NO shows up.
cols.YEAR_FILING_FOR: The year the OSHA injury report covers, like 2023. Each table holds one year.

cols.CASE_NUMBER: The agency's ID number for one case. The format depends on the agency, like 09-2024-0639 or I-200-19058-315794.
cols.JOB_DESCRIPTION: The injured worker's job title as the employer typed it, like Warehouse Associate or RN.
cols.SOC_CODE: The job's standard occupation code, like 29-1141 for registered nurses. Some OSHA rows hold junk like 9999 or 2598276.
cols.SOC_DESCRIPTION: The injured worker's job sorted into the government's standard job category, like Registered Nurses. Uncoded means it could not be matched.
cols.SOC_REVIEWED: A 0, 1 or 2 flag about whether the worker's job code was reviewed. What each number means needs OSHA's lookup.
cols.SOC_PROBABILITY: How confident the automatic job-category match was, from 0 to 1. Stored as text; odd values like 5 show up.
cols.DATE_OF_INCIDENT: The date the worker was hurt or got sick.
cols.INCIDENT_OUTCOME: How bad the case got, as a code: 1 death, 2 days away from work, 3 light duty or job transfer, 4 other recordable case.
cols.DAFW_NUM_AWAY: How many days the injured worker was kept home from work.
cols.DJTR_NUM_TR: How many days the injured worker spent on light duty or in another job.
cols.TYPE_OF_INCIDENT: What kind of case it was, as a code: 1 injury, 2 skin illness, 3 breathing illness, 4 poisoning, 5 hearing loss, 6 other illness.
cols.TIME_STARTED_WORK: What time the worker started their shift that day, as text. 2023 writes 7:00:00.000; later years write 7:00. Sometimes blank.
cols.TIME_OF_INCIDENT: What time of day the worker got hurt, as text. 2023 writes 20:00:00.000; later years write 20:00. Sometimes blank.
cols.TIME_UNKNOWN: Whether the time of the incident is unknown: 1 yes, 0 no.
cols.DATE_OF_DEATH: The date the worker died, if the case was fatal. Almost always blank.

cols.NEW_NAR_WHAT_HAPPENED: The employer's own words on how the injury happened. Names are replaced with [REDACTED].
cols.NEW_NAR_BEFORE_INCIDENT: The employer's own words on what the worker was doing just before getting hurt. Names are replaced with [REDACTED].
cols.NEW_INCIDENT_LOCATION: Where at the workplace it happened, in the employer's words, like Emergency Room or Decant line 1 station 12.
cols.NEW_NAR_INJURY_ILLNESS: The employer's own words on the injury and the body part hurt, like Left knee sprain.
cols.NEW_NAR_OBJECT_SUBSTANCE: The object or substance that hurt the worker, in the employer's words, like Pallet or needle. Junk like blank and n a shows up.
cols.NEW_INCIDENT_DESCRIPTION: A short summary of the incident in the employer's words, like Tripped over a pallet. Names are replaced with [REDACTED].

cols.NID: The Federal Judicial Center's ID number for a federal judge.

cols.APPOINTMENT_TITLE: The judge's title in that seat, like Judge, Chief Judge or Associate Justice.
cols.APPOINTING_PRESIDENT: The president who appointed the judge. "None - assignment" style values mean the judge was moved, not appointed.
cols.PARTY_OF_APPOINTING_PRESIDENT: The appointing president's party, like Democratic or Republican. Starts with "None" for reassignments.

cols.HEARING_DATE: The date of the hearing: the court's hearing in appeals cases, the Senate hearing in judge records. Often blank.
cols.AYES_NAYS: The Senate vote count on the judge, yes/no, like "53/43". Blank for voice votes; one table adds a leading space.

cols.COMMISSION_DATE: The date the judge was formally commissioned into the seat. Text in one table, a real date in the other.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE: The date the thing ended, like a registration, recall, or judge's service. Empty when it has not ended.

cols.CONGRESS: Which Congress, by number, like 118. Each Congress lasts two years.
cols.BILL_TYPE: The kind of bill as a short code: HR is a House bill, S a Senate bill, HRES and SRES are resolutions, and so on.
cols.BILL_NUMBER: The bill's number. Some tables store only the number, like 4210; others add the type, like HR5326 or HRES643.
cols.INTRODUCED_DATE: The date the bill was introduced in Congress.
cols.SPONSOR_BIOGUIDE: The bill sponsor's Congress biography ID, like P000614. Use it to match members across tables.
cols.LAW_NUMBER: The public law number if the bill became law, as Congress-number, like 118-263. Blank for bills that did not pass.
cols.N_ACTIONS: How many steps the bill has gone through in Congress. Stored as text in one table.
cols.LATEST_ACTION_DATE: The date of the most recent step on the bill. Stored as text in one table.
cols.LATEST_ACTION_TEXT: The most recent step on the bill, in words, like "Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary".
cols.N_COSPONSORS: How many members signed on as cosponsors of the bill. Stored as text in one table.

cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas. Some tables write it in capitals.

cols.STATE_FIPS: The state's two-digit number code, like 06 for California. One table drops the leading zero, so 1 means 01.
cols.STAGE: The election stage: gen for the general election, pre for a primary.
cols.CANDIDATE_NAME: The candidate's name as printed in the election results. Styles vary: Carter, Jimmy in one table, ALLAN NORWITZ in another, NA in some rows.
cols.IS_WRITEIN: Whether the candidate was a write-in: True or False.
cols.VOTE_MODE: How the votes were cast. Always "total" in the sampled rows, meaning all modes combined.
cols.CANDIDATE_VOTES: How many votes the candidate got in that race.
cols.VOTE_SHARE: The candidate's share of the vote as a decimal, so 0.55 means 55 percent.
cols.IS_SPECIAL_ELECTION: True if it was a special election to fill an open seat. False in every sampled row.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.CONGRESS: Which Congress, by number, like 118. Each Congress lasts two years.
cols.CHAMBER: Which chamber of Congress: House or Senate. Some tables write rep or sen, and one also has President.
cols.ROLLNUMBER: The number of the roll-call vote, counting up from 1 within each Congress and chamber. Pair it with the Congress number to find one vote.
cols.SESSION: Which session of that Congress the vote fell in, 1 or 2.
cols.VOTE_RESULT: How the vote came out, like Passed or Failed. For votes electing the Speaker it holds the winner's name, like Jeffries.
cols.VOTE_QUESTION: The question put to the vote, like "On Motion to Recommit".
cols.BILL_NUMBER: The bill's number. Some tables store only the number, like 4210; others add the type, like HR5326 or HRES643.
cols.VOTE_DESC: A short description of what was being voted on, like the bill's title. Often blank.

cols.CONGRESS: Which Congress, by number, like 118. Each Congress lasts two years.
cols.CHAMBER: Which chamber of Congress: House or Senate. Some tables write rep or sen, and one also has President.
cols.ROLLNUMBER: The number of the roll-call vote, counting up from 1 within each Congress and chamber. Pair it with the Congress number to find one vote.
cols.ICPSR: The member of Congress's ICPSR number, a standard ID used by the Voteview voting data. Use it to join member tables.

cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. Some tables store it as text and a few use a range like 2000-2002.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.VOTE_SHARE: The candidate's share of the vote as a decimal, so 0.55 means 55 percent.
cols.BIOGUIDE: The member of Congress's official ID, a letter and six digits like A000383.
cols.SPINE_NAME: The member of Congress's name as spelled in the warehouse's master member list, like Ron Wyden.
cols.ICPSR: The member of Congress's ICPSR number, a standard ID used by the Voteview voting data. Use it to join member tables.
cols.MATCH_METHOD: How this row was matched to another list, like exact, fuzzy, or by name plus state.

cols.UNNAMED_0: A leftover row number from how the file was saved, counting 1, 2, 3. It means nothing about the data.
cols.NAME: The name of the person, company, or charity the row is about. People are often written last name first, and spelling is not cleaned.
cols.CIRCUIT: The federal appeals court region, numbered 1 to 11. Some tables add a leading zero, like 05.
cols.JCS: The judge's ideology score on the Judicial Common Space scale, from about -1 liberal to +1 conservative. Stored as text in two tables.

cols.UNNAMED_0: A leftover row number from how the file was saved, counting 1, 2, 3. It means nothing about the data.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. Some tables store it as text and a few use a range like 2000-2002.
cols.CONGRESS: Which Congress, by number, like 118. Each Congress lasts two years.
cols.HOUSE_MEDIAN: The ideology score of the middle member of the House that year; below zero leans liberal, above leans conservative. Text in one table.
cols.SENATE_MEDIAN: The ideology score of the middle member of the Senate that year; below zero leans liberal, above leans conservative. Text in one table.
cols.SC_MEDIAN: The ideology score of the middle Supreme Court justice that year. Missing years are blank in one table and the text "NA" in the other.

cols.UNNAMED_0: A leftover row number from how the file was saved, counting 1, 2, 3. It means nothing about the data.
cols.JCS: The judge's ideology score on the Judicial Common Space scale, from about -1 liberal to +1 conservative. Stored as text in two tables.

cols.ENTITY: The country or region name, like Albania or World.
cols.YEAR: The year the row covers, like 2021. Some tables store it as text and a few use a range like 2000-2002.
cols.WORLD_REGION_ACCORDING_TO_OWID: The continent the country belongs to, as Our World in Data groups them, like Europe or Africa.

cols.SAM_NUMBER: The federal contracting system's own ID for this exclusion record, a long random-looking code.
cols.UEI: The 12-character Unique Entity ID the federal government gives each business, which replaced DUNS. Often blank.
cols.CAGE_CODE: The contractor's five-character Defense Department vendor code, like 1L027. Blank for many rows in some tables.
cols.NPI: The doctor's or clinic's 10-digit Medicare provider number, the National Provider Identifier. Stored as text.
cols.ENTITY_NAME: The name of the company, person, or group the record is about.
cols.FIRST_NAME: The person's first name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.LAST_NAME: The person's last name. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.EXCLUSION_TYPE: Why the person or company is barred. HHS tables use the law section as a code like 1128a1; the SAM tables use words like Voluntary Exclusion.
cols.EXCLUSION_PROGRAM: What the ban covers: Procurement, NonProcurement, or Reciprocal.
cols.EXCLUDING_AGENCY: The federal agency that barred the person or company, as a short abbreviation like HHS, DOJ, or EPA.
cols.ACTIVATION_DATE: The date the ban took effect.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE_RAW: The date the ban ends, or the word Indefinite. Stored as text, so it will not sort as a date.
cols.TERMINATION_DATE: The date the thing ended, like a registration, recall, or judge's service. Empty when it has not ended.
cols.RECORD_STATUS: Whether the record is live at the source. Always Published in the device table and Active in the exclusions table.
cols.CITY: The city or town name. Mostly in capitals, sometimes mixed case, and spellings are not cleaned.
cols.STATE: The state, as two letters like TX or PR. Some tables leave it empty.
cols.ZIP: The ZIP code, stored as text so leading zeros survive. Often 9 digits with a dash, and 00000 shows up as a blank.
cols.COUNTRY: The country. Written different ways by table: a full name, a two- or three-letter code, or a number code that needs a lookup.
cols.IS_CURRENTLY_EXCLUDED: True if the ban is still in force, False if it has ended.
cols.IS_ENTITY_NOT_INDIVIDUAL: True if the barred party is a business or group, False if it is a person.
cols._LOADED_AT: When this row was loaded into the warehouse. Usually a date and time, but some tables store it as a long number counting microseconds since 1970. Added by your pipeline, not the source.

cols.CONTRACT_TRANSACTION_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's ID for one contract action, built from agency codes, the contract number and the change number joined by underscores. -NONE- fills empty parts.
cols.CONTRACT_AWARD_UNIQUE_KEY: USAspending's own key for the whole contract, built from the contract number and agency code, like CONT_AWD_FA527023F0101_9700.
cols.AWARD_ID_PIID: The government's contract number, like FA527023F0101.
cols.MODIFICATION_NUMBER: Which change to the award this row is, with 0 for the original. Formats are messy: 0, 0000 and P00003 all appear.
cols.TRANSACTION_NUMBER: A number that tells apart contract actions that would otherwise look the same. Almost always 0.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_AGENCY_ID: The 4-digit code of the agency that owns the umbrella contract this order falls under, like 3600 for Veterans Affairs. Blank when there is no umbrella contract.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_AGENCY_NAME: The name of the agency that owns the umbrella contract this order falls under. Spelling varies, like DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS versus VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_ID_PIID: The contract number of the umbrella contract this order falls under, like GS03FGA010. Blank when there is none.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_MODIFICATION_NUMBER: Which change to the umbrella contract this refers to, like P00006 or 0 for the original.
cols.FEDERAL_ACTION_OBLIGATION: The dollars the government committed or took back in this one transaction. Negative numbers are cuts or cancellations.
cols.TOTAL_DOLLARS_OBLIGATED: The total dollars the government has committed to the whole contract so far, across all its transactions. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.TOTAL_OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FOR_OVERALL_AWARD: Total dollars actually paid out on the whole award so far. Almost always blank.
cols.BASE_AND_EXERCISED_OPTIONS_VALUE: The dollar value the government has committed to so far, the base deal plus any extra options it chose to use. Can be negative when a change cuts it.
cols.CURRENT_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: What the whole contract is currently worth in dollars, counting options already used. Blank in many rows of the older tables.
cols.BASE_AND_ALL_OPTIONS_VALUE: The dollar value if the government used every option in the contract. Can be negative when a change cuts it.
cols.POTENTIAL_TOTAL_VALUE_OF_AWARD: The most the whole contract could be worth in dollars. Mostly blank in the older contracts table.
cols.DISASTER_EMERGENCY_FUND_CODES_FOR_OVERAL: Which emergency spending law funded the award, as a code plus words, like Q: Not Designated or Z: Emergency P.L. 117-58. Blank in two of the three tables.
cols.OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FROM_COVID_19_SUPPLEMENT: Dollars paid out on the award from COVID-19 relief money. Nearly always blank.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT_FROM_COVID_19_SUPPLEMEN: Dollars promised to the award from COVID-19 relief money. Nearly always blank, and can be negative after a cut.
cols.OUTLAYED_AMOUNT_FROM_IIJA_SUPPLEMENTAL_F: Dollars paid out on the award from the 2021 infrastructure law money. Nearly always blank.
cols.OBLIGATED_AMOUNT_FROM_IIJA_SUPPLEMENTAL_: Dollars promised to the award from the 2021 infrastructure law money. Nearly always blank.
cols.ACTION_DATE: The date of the award action, like a new contract or a change to one. Two tables store it as text.
cols.ACTION_DATE_FISCAL_YEAR: The federal fiscal year of the transaction, like 2007. Federal fiscal years start October 1.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_START_DATE: The date the work or grant was set to begin. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_CURRENT_END_DATE: The date the work or grant is currently set to end, which can be in the future. Some tables store it as text.
cols.PERIOD_OF_PERFORMANCE_POTENTIAL_END_DATE: The latest date the work could run to if every option is used.
cols.ORDERING_PERIOD_END_DATE: The last date agencies can place orders under this umbrella contract. Mostly blank.
cols.SOLICITATION_DATE: The date the government asked for bids.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_CODE: The three-digit code for the federal department that made the award, like 036. Stored as text to keep the leading zero.
cols.AWARDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency that made the award, like Department of Defense.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_CODE: The four-character code for the office inside the department that made the award, like 3600. Some contain letters, like 12K3.
cols.AWARDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The office inside the agency that gave the award, like Department of the Navy or National Park Service.
cols.AWARDING_OFFICE_CODE: The code for the contracting office that made the award, like 47QSSC. Blank in the grants table.
cols.AWARDING_OFFICE_NAME: The name of the contracting office that made the award. Blank in the grants table.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_CODE: The three-digit code for the federal department paying for the award, like 047. Blank in the grants table.
cols.FUNDING_AGENCY_NAME: The federal agency whose money paid for the award. Can differ from the agency that made it.
cols.FUNDING_SUB_AGENCY_CODE: The four-character code for the office inside the department paying for the award. Blank in the grants table.
cols.FUNDING_SUB_AGENCY_NAME: The name of the office inside the department paying for the award, like Department of the Navy. Blank in the grants table.
cols.FUNDING_OFFICE_CODE: The code for the office paying for the award, like N68732. Blank in the grants table.
cols.FUNDING_OFFICE_NAME: The name of the office paying for the award. Blank in the grants table.
cols.TREASURY_ACCOUNTS_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The Treasury accounts that paid for the award, as codes like 086-X-0303-000, several split by semicolons. Mostly blank.
cols.FEDERAL_ACCOUNTS_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The federal budget accounts that paid for the award, like 086-0303, several split by semicolons. Mostly blank.
cols.OBJECT_CLASSES_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: What kind of spending paid for it, as a budget category code plus words, like 31.0: Equipment. Mostly blank.
cols.PROGRAM_ACTIVITIES_FUNDING_THIS_AWARD: The budget programs that paid for the award, as a code plus words, like 0001: SPACE OPERATIONS. Mostly blank.
cols.FOREIGN_FUNDING: Whether foreign money paid for the contract, as a letter: A foreign military sales, B other foreign funds, X not applicable.
cols.FOREIGN_FUNDING_DESCRIPTION: Whether foreign money paid for the contract, in words: NOT APPLICABLE, FOREIGN FUNDS FMS for foreign military sales, or FOREIGN FUNDS NON-FMS.
cols.SAM_EXCEPTION: A code for why the contractor did not have to register in the federal vendor system, SAM. Almost always blank.
cols.SAM_EXCEPTION_DESCRIPTION: Why the contractor did not have to register in SAM, the federal vendor system, in words like AWARDS TO FOREIGN ENTITIES. Almost always blank; some rows hold stray letters.
cols.RECIPIENT_UEI: The recipient's 12-character federal ID, the Unique Entity ID that replaced the DUNS number.
cols.RECIPIENT_DUNS: The recipient's old 9-digit DUNS business number. 000000000 means none, and newer tables leave it empty.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME: Who received the money, like a company, agency, or campaign.
cols.RECIPIENT_NAME_RAW: The award recipient's name exactly as the source wrote it, not cleaned up.
cols.RECIPIENT_DOING_BUSINESS_AS_NAME: The trade name the contractor goes by, if different from its legal name. Blank for most rows.
cols.CAGE_CODE: The contractor's five-character Defense Department vendor code, like 1L027. Blank for many rows in some tables.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_UEI: The 12-character federal ID of the recipient's parent company. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_DUNS: The 9-digit DUNS number, the old business ID, of the recipient's parent company.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, in capitals. Often blank in the grants table.
cols.RECIPIENT_PARENT_NAME_RAW: The name of the recipient's parent company or government, exactly as the source wrote it.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_CODE: The recipient's country, usually a three-letter code like USA. Older contract rows spell out names like JAPAN instead.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTRY_NAME: The country where the recipient is based, in capitals. The US shows up as both UNITED STATES and UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.
cols.RECIPIENT_ADDRESS_LINE_1: The first line of the recipient's street address.
cols.RECIPIENT_ADDRESS_LINE_2: The second line of the recipient's address, like a suite number. Mostly blank, with junk like 0 or N/A.
cols.RECIPIENT_CITY_NAME: The city where the recipient is based, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_COUNTY: The recipient's 5-digit county code. Broken in the grants table: stored like 4243.0, with a decimal added and leading zeros lost.
cols.RECIPIENT_COUNTY_NAME: The recipient's county name, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_STATE_: The recipient's state as a 2-digit code, like 06 for California. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_CODE: The recipient's state, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.RECIPIENT_STATE_NAME: The recipient's state spelled out, like MARYLAND.
cols.RECIPIENT_ZIP_4_CODE: The contractor's full nine-digit zip code, usually with no dash. Leading zeros can be lost.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_CD_ORI: The recipient's congressional district when the award was made, as state and number like MD-06.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_RECIPIENT_CD_CUR: The recipient's congressional district under today's district lines, as state and number like MD-06.
cols.RECIPIENT_PHONE_NUMBER: The contractor's phone number, 10 digits with no dashes, stored as text.
cols.RECIPIENT_FAX_NUMBER: The contractor's fax number, 10 digits with no dashes, stored as text.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTRY_COD: The country where the work is done, as a three-letter code like USA.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTRY_NAM: The country where the work is done, spelled out, like UNITED STATES.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_CITY_NAME: The city where the work was actually done, in capitals. Can differ from where the recipient is based.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The 5-digit county code where the work is done, like 06037 for Los Angeles. Keep it as text for the leading zero.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_COUNTY_NAME: The county where the work is done, in capitals.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The state where the work is done, as a 2-digit code like 06 for California.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_CODE: The state where the work was actually done, as two letters. Territories like GU for Guam appear too.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_STATE_NAME: The state where the work is done, spelled out.
cols.PRIMARY_PLACE_OF_PERFORMANCE_ZIP_4: The ZIP code where the work is done: 9 digits when the extra four are known, 5 otherwise. Keep it as text for leading zeros.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_TRANSACTION_PLACE_OF_PERFORM: The congressional district where the work is done, when the award was made, like CA-28. Some grant rows hold only the number, like 02.
The congressional district where the work is done, under today's district lines, like CA-28.
cols.AWARD_OR_IDV_FLAG: Whether the row is a regular contract, AWARD, or an umbrella deal other orders are placed under, IDV.
cols.AWARD_TYPE_CODE: What kind of contract it is, as a letter A to D, like a purchase order or delivery order. Needs a lookup.
cols.AWARD_TYPE: What kind of award: a contract type like PURCHASE ORDER or DELIVERY ORDER, or a grant type. Some rows use short forms like PO or DO, and the NIH table uses a one-digit code.
cols.IDV_TYPE_CODE: What kind of umbrella deal it is, as a letter A to E. Needs a lookup; blank for regular contracts.
cols.IDV_TYPE: What kind of umbrella deal it is, as a short name like IDC, BPA, FSS or GWAC. Blank for regular contracts.
cols.MULTIPLE_OR_SINGLE_AWARD_IDV_CODE: Whether the umbrella deal went to one company or several: S single, M multiple. Mostly blank.
cols.MULTIPLE_OR_SINGLE_AWARD_IDV: Whether the umbrella deal went to one company or several: SINGLE AWARD or MULTIPLE AWARD. Mostly blank.
cols.TYPE_OF_IDC_CODE: For open-ended delivery contracts, how the amount is set, as a letter A, B or C. Nearly always blank.
cols.TYPE_OF_IDC: For open-ended delivery contracts, how the amount is set, like INDEFINITE DELIVERY / INDEFINITE QUANTITY. Nearly always blank.
cols.TYPE_OF_CONTRACT_PRICING_CODE: How the contract price is set, as a one-character code like J for firm fixed price. Needs a lookup.
cols.TYPE_OF_CONTRACT_PRICING: How the contract price is set, in words like FIRM FIXED PRICE, COST PLUS FIXED FEE or TIME AND MATERIALS.
cols.TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: A free-text note on what was bought or funded, often full of internal codes and abbreviations.
cols.PRIME_AWARD_BASE_TRANSACTION_DESCRIPTION: What the award is for, in the agency's own free-text words.
cols.ACTION_TYPE: What kind of change this contract action was, in words, like CHANGE ORDER, FUNDING ONLY ACTION or CLOSE OUT. Mostly blank.
cols.SOLICITATION_IDENTIFIER: The government's ID for the request for bids that led to this contract, like N0002406R5430. Mostly blank.
cols.NUMBER_OF_ACTIONS: How many contract actions this row stands for. Almost always 1.
cols.INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS: A code for whether the work is close to jobs only government should do: CL, CT, OT, or a combo like CL,CT. The words are in INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS_DESCRIPTION.
cols.INHERENTLY_GOVERNMENTAL_FUNCTIONS_DESCRI: Whether the work is close to jobs only government should do, in words, like CLOSELY ASSOCIATED, CRITICAL FUNCTIONS or OTHER FUNCTIONS.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE: A four-character code for what was bought, like 7110 or R499. All-number codes are goods, letter-first codes are services; needs a lookup.
cols.PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_CODE_DESCRIPTION: What kind of thing the government bought, in capitals, like OFFICE SUPPLIES or DRUGS AND BIOLOGICALS.
cols.CONTRACT_BUNDLING_CODE: A short code for whether several needs were bundled into one contract, like D, C or H. The words for it are in CONTRACT_BUNDLING.
cols.CONTRACT_BUNDLING: Whether several needs were bundled into one contract, in words, like NOT A BUNDLED REQUIREMENT or NOT BUNDLED.
cols.DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_CODE: A short code for the Defense Department spending category, like A3, C9E or S1. The words for it are in DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION.
cols.DOD_CLAIMANT_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION: The Defense Department spending category in words, like SHIPS, SERVICES or COMBAT VEHICLES.
cols.NAICS_CODE: The six-digit industry code, like 722110 for restaurants. Needs a lookup to read; 000000 means not given.
cols.NAICS_DESCRIPTION: The industry in words, like Full-Service Restaurants. It goes with the six-digit NAICS code.
cols.RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY_CODE: A short code for which recycled-material or green-buying clauses the contract has, like A, B or C. The words for it are in RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY.
cols.RECOVERED_MATERIALS_SUSTAINABILITY: Which recycled-material or green-buying clauses the contract has, in words, like FAR 52.223-4 INCLUDED or BIO-BASED. Some values are cut off mid-word.
cols.DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY_CODE: A short code for whether the contractor is U.S. or foreign owned, like A, C or D. The words for it are in DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY.
cols.DOMESTIC_OR_FOREIGN_ENTITY: Whether the contractor is U.S. or foreign owned, in words, like U.S. OWNED BUSINESS or FOREIGN-OWNED BUSINESS NOT INCORPORATED IN THE U.S.
cols.DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_CODE: A short code for the Defense weapons or buying program, like 234, DAL or 000. The words for it are in DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION.
cols.DOD_ACQUISITION_PROGRAM_DESCRIPTION: The Defense weapons or buying program in words, like STRYKER or M1/M1A1 ABRAMS TANK. Almost always blank.
cols.INFORMATION_TECHNOLOGY_COMMERCIAL_ITEM_C: A short code for what kind of tech purchase this was, like Z, A or E. The words for it are in INFORMATION_TECHNOLOGY_COMMERCIAL_ITEM_CATEGORY.
What kind of tech purchase this was, in words, like NOT IT PRODUCTS OR SERVICES or COMMERCIAL SERVICE.
cols.EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT_CODE: A short code for whether the goods had to meet EPA recycled-content rules, like A or E. The words for it are in EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT.
cols.EPA_DESIGNATED_PRODUCT: Whether the goods had to meet EPA recycled-content rules, in words, like MEETS REQUIREMENTS or NOT REQUIRED.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_ORIGIN_COD: The country the goods or services came from, as a three-letter code like USA, DEU or IRQ.
cols.COUNTRY_OF_PRODUCT_OR_SERVICE_ORIGIN: The country the goods or services came from, spelled out, like UNITED STATES or IRAQ.
cols.PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE_CODE: A short code for where the goods were made, like C, D or G. The words for it are in PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE.
cols.PLACE_OF_MANUFACTURE: Where the goods were made, in words, like MFG IN U.S. or NOT A MANUFACTURED END PRODUCT. Some values are cut off.
cols.SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN_CODE: A short code for whether the contractor needed a plan to pass work to small businesses, like A, B or F. The words for it are in SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN.
cols.SUBCONTRACTING_PLAN: Whether the contractor needed a plan to pass work to small businesses, in words, like PLAN NOT REQUIRED.
cols.EXTENT_COMPETED_CODE: A short code for how much competition there was for the contract, like A, B, D or G. The words for it are in EXTENT_COMPETED.
cols.EXTENT_COMPETED: How much competition there was for the contract, in words, like FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION or NOT COMPETED.
cols.SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES_CODE: A short code for how bids were asked for, like SP1, NP or SSS. The words for it are in SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES.
cols.SOLICITATION_PROCEDURES: How bids were asked for, in words, like SIMPLIFIED ACQUISITION, SEALED BID or ONLY ONE SOURCE.
cols.TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE_CODE: A short code for which kind of business the contract was reserved for, like SBA, 8A or SDVOSBC. The words for it are in TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE.
cols.TYPE_OF_SET_ASIDE: Which kind of business the contract was reserved for, in words, like NO SET ASIDE USED. or HUBZONE SET-ASIDE.
cols.EVALUATED_PREFERENCE_CODE: A short code for a price edge given to certain small businesses, like SPS. Almost always blank.
cols.EVALUATED_PREFERENCE: Whether certain small businesses got a price edge when bids were judged, in words. Almost always NO PREFERENCE USED.
cols.RESEARCH_CODE: A short code for the small-business research program and phase, like SR1 or ST1. The words for it are in RESEARCH.
cols.RESEARCH: The small-business research program and phase in words, like SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH PROGRAM PHASE II ACTION. Almost always blank.
cols.FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES_CODE: A short code for why an order under an existing contract was or was not opened to other holders, like FAIR, ONE or FOO. The words for it are in FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES.
cols.FAIR_OPPORTUNITY_LIMITED_SOURCES: Why an order under an existing contract was or was not opened to other holders, in words, like FAIR OPPORTUNITY GIVEN or URGENCY.
cols.OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION_COD: A short code for the legal reason the contract skipped open bidding, like UNQ, OTH or ONE. The words for it are in OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION.
cols.OTHER_THAN_FULL_AND_OPEN_COMPETITION: The legal reason the contract skipped open bidding, in words, like UNIQUE SOURCE or AUTHORIZED BY STATUTE.
cols.NUMBER_OF_OFFERS_RECEIVED: How many bids came in. A 999 shows up and is likely filler, not a real count.
cols.COMMERCIAL_ITEM_ACQUISITION_PROCEDURES_C: A short code for whether off-the-shelf buying rules were used, like A, B or D. The words for it are in COMMERCIAL_ITEM_ACQUISITION_PROCEDURES.
cols.COMMERCIAL_ITEM_ACQUISITION_PROCEDURES: Whether off-the-shelf buying rules were used, in words, like COMMERCIAL ITEM or COMMERCIAL ITEM PROCEDURES NOT USED. The wording changed over time.
cols.SMALL_BUSINESS_COMPETITIVENESS_DEMONSTRA: Whether the contract fell under a small-business pilot program, as t or f. Always f where filled.
cols.SIMPLIFIED_PROCEDURES_FOR_CERTAIN_COMMER: Whether a shortcut buying process for commercial goods was used, as Y or N.
Whether a shortcut buying process for commercial goods was used, as YES or NO.
cols.A76_FAIR_ACT_ACTION_CODE: Whether the work came out of a review of jobs government could hand to contractors. Mixes N, NO and YES in one column.
cols.A76_FAIR_ACT_ACTION: Whether the work came out of a review of jobs government could hand to contractors, as YES or NO. Almost always NO.
cols.FED_BIZ_OPPS_CODE: Whether the opportunity was posted on the federal bid website: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.FED_BIZ_OPPS: Whether the opportunity was posted on the federal bid website, as YES, NO or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.LOCAL_AREA_SET_ASIDE_CODE: Whether the contract was reserved for local businesses in a disaster area, as Y or N.
cols.LOCAL_AREA_SET_ASIDE: Whether the contract was reserved for local businesses in a disaster area, as YES or NO.
cols.PRICE_EVALUATION_ADJUSTMENT_PREFERENCE_P: The percent price edge given to a favored bidder. Always 0 where filled; mostly blank.
cols.CLINGER_COHEN_ACT_PLANNING_CODE: Whether the tech buy followed federal IT planning rules. Mixes plain N and Y with N: NO and Y: YES.
cols.CLINGER_COHEN_ACT_PLANNING: Whether the tech buy followed federal IT planning rules, as YES or NO.
cols.MATERIALS_SUPPLIES_ARTICLES_EQUIPMENT_CO: Whether the federal wage law for goods contracts applies: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.MATERIALS_SUPPLIES_ARTICLES_EQUIPMENT: Whether the federal wage law for goods contracts applies, as YES, NO or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.LABOR_STANDARDS_CODE: Whether federal wage rules for service workers apply: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.LABOR_STANDARDS: Whether federal wage rules for service workers apply, as YES, NO or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.CONSTRUCTION_WAGE_RATE_REQUIREMENTS_CODE: Whether local-wage rules for construction workers apply: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.CONSTRUCTION_WAGE_RATE_REQUIREMENTS: Whether local-wage rules for construction workers apply, as YES, NO or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.INTERAGENCY_CONTRACTING_AUTHORITY_CODE: The law that let one agency buy for another: A, B, or X for not applicable. The words are in INTERAGENCY_CONTRACTING_AUTHORITY.
cols.INTERAGENCY_CONTRACTING_AUTHORITY: The law that let one agency buy for another, in words, like ECONOMY ACT, OTHER STATUTORY AUTHORITY or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.OTHER_STATUTORY_AUTHORITY: The law cited when one agency bought for another under something other than the Economy Act, as free text like 40 U.S.C. 321. Almost always blank.
cols.PROGRAM_ACRONYM: The short name of the government-wide contract program used, like SEWP V or GWAC-VETS 2. Almost always blank.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_TYPE_CODE: A short code for the type of umbrella contract this order was placed under, like A, B or C. The words for it are in PARENT_AWARD_TYPE.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_TYPE: The type of umbrella contract this order was placed under, as an acronym like IDC, BPA, FSS or GWAC. Blank when there is no umbrella contract.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_SINGLE_OR_MULTIPLE_CODE: Whether the umbrella contract went to one company or several: S for single, M for multiple.
cols.PARENT_AWARD_SINGLE_OR_MULTIPLE: Whether the umbrella contract went to one company or several: SINGLE AWARD or MULTIPLE AWARD.
cols.MAJOR_PROGRAM: A program name typed in by the agency, free text like VETERANS FIRST CONTRACTING or JANSAN FSSI. Messy and mostly blank.
cols.NATIONAL_INTEREST_ACTION_CODE: A code for the national emergency the buy was tied to, like H05K. Almost always blank.
cols.NATIONAL_INTEREST_ACTION: The national emergency the buy was tied to, like HURRICANE KATRINA 2005. Almost always blank.
cols.COST_OR_PRICING_DATA_CODE: Whether the contractor had to hand over detailed cost data: Y, N, or W for waived.
cols.COST_OR_PRICING_DATA: Whether the contractor had to hand over detailed cost data, as YES, NO or NOT OBTAINED - WAIVED.
cols.COST_ACCOUNTING_STANDARDS_CLAUSE_CODE: Whether federal cost-accounting rules apply: Y, N, or X for exempt.
cols.COST_ACCOUNTING_STANDARDS_CLAUSE: Whether federal cost-accounting rules apply, in words, like YES - CAS CLAUSE INCLUDED or NOT APPLICABLE EXEMPT FROM CAS.
cols.GOVERNMENT_FURNISHED_PROPERTY_CODE: Whether the government lent the contractor equipment or property, as Y or N.
cols.GOVERNMENT_FURNISHED_PROPERTY: Whether the government lent the contractor equipment or property, in words: TRANSACTION USES GFE/GFP or TRANSACTION DOES NOT USE GFE/GFP.
cols.SEA_TRANSPORTATION_CODE: Whether goods were expected to ship by sea: Y, N, or U for unknown.
cols.SEA_TRANSPORTATION: Whether goods were expected to ship by sea, as YES, NO or UNKNOWN.
cols.UNDEFINITIZED_ACTION_CODE: Whether work started before the final terms were set: X, N, A or B. The words are in UNDEFINITIZED_ACTION.
cols.UNDEFINITIZED_ACTION: Whether work started before the final terms were set, in words, like NO, LETTER CONTRACT or OTHER UNDEFINITIZED ACTION.
cols.CONSOLIDATED_CONTRACT_CODE: Whether several needs were merged into one contract. The code set changed: Y or N in one table, D, N or B in the other.
cols.CONSOLIDATED_CONTRACT: Whether several needs were merged into one contract, in words, like NO, YES or NOT CONSOLIDATED.
cols.PERFORMANCE_BASED_SERVICE_ACQUISITION_CO: Whether the service contract pays for results rather than hours: Y, N, or X for not applicable.
cols.PERFORMANCE_BASED_SERVICE_ACQUISITION: Whether the service contract pays for results rather than hours, in words, like YES - SERVICE WHERE PBA IS USED. or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.MULTI_YEAR_CONTRACT_CODE: Whether the contract covers several years of needs up front, as Y or N.
cols.MULTI_YEAR_CONTRACT: Whether the contract covers several years of needs up front, as YES or NO.
cols.CONTRACT_FINANCING_CODE: A short code for how the contractor gets paid before the work is done, like A, E or Z. The words for it are in CONTRACT_FINANCING.
cols.CONTRACT_FINANCING: How the contractor gets paid before the work is done, in words, like FAR 52.232-16 PROGRESS PAYMENTS or NOT APPLICABLE.
cols.PURCHASE_CARD_AS_PAYMENT_METHOD_CODE: Whether it was paid with a government credit card, as Y or N.
cols.PURCHASE_CARD_AS_PAYMENT_METHOD: Whether it was paid with a government credit card, as YES or NO.
cols.CONTINGENCY_HUMANITARIAN_OR_PEACEKEEPING: Whether the buy supported a disaster, humanitarian or peacekeeping operation: B, C, or X for not applicable.
Whether the buy supported a disaster, humanitarian or peacekeeping operation, in words. Mostly NOT APPLICABLE; some values are cut off.
cols.ALASKAN_NATIVE_CORPORATION_OWNED_FIRM: Whether the contractor is owned by an Alaska Native corporation, as t or f.
cols.AMERICAN_INDIAN_OWNED_BUSINESS: Whether the contractor is American Indian owned, as t or f.
cols.INDIAN_TRIBE_FEDERALLY_RECOGNIZED: Whether the contractor is a federally recognized Indian tribe, as t or f.
cols.NATIVE_HAWAIIAN_ORGANIZATION_OWNED_FIRM: Whether the contractor is owned by a Native Hawaiian organization, as t or f.
cols.TRIBALLY_OWNED_FIRM: Whether the contractor is owned by a tribe, as t or f.
cols.VETERAN_OWNED_BUSINESS: Whether the contractor is veteran owned, as t or f.
cols.SERVICE_DISABLED_VETERAN_OWNED_BUSINESS: Whether the contractor is owned by a veteran disabled in service, as t or f.
cols.WOMAN_OWNED_BUSINESS: Whether the contractor is woman owned, as t or f.
cols.WOMEN_OWNED_SMALL_BUSINESS: Whether the contractor is certified as a woman-owned small business, as t or f.
cols.ECONOMICALLY_DISADVANTAGED_WOMEN_OWNED_S: Whether the contractor is certified as an economically disadvantaged woman-owned small business, as t or f.
cols.JOINT_VENTURE_WOMEN_OWNED_SMALL_BUSINESS: Whether the contractor is a joint venture counted as a woman-owned small business, as t or f.
cols.JOINT_VENTURE_ECONOMIC_DISADVANTAGED_WOM: Whether the contractor is a joint venture counted as an economically disadvantaged woman-owned small business, as t or f.

cols.INCIDENT_MONTH: The month of the incident as two digits, like 08. Stored as text.
cols.OTHER_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code of a second railroad involved, like CSX. Almost always blank.
cols.OTHER_RAILROAD_NAME: The name of a second railroad involved. Almost always blank.
cols.MAINTENANCE_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code of the railroad that maintains the track, like NS or CSX.
cols.MAINTENANCE_RAILROAD_NAME: The name of the railroad that maintains the track, like Norfolk Southern Railway Company.
cols.GRADE_CROSSING_ID: The national ID of the road-rail crossing, six digits and a letter, like 630474Y. Mostly blank in the equipment accidents table.
cols.MONTH: The month. Formats vary a lot: January, 08, 2023-09, 01-1987, a mid-month date, or Total.
cols.DAY: The day of the month as two digits, like 09. Stored as text.
cols.SUBDIVISION: The railroad's name for its stretch of line, like PIEDMONT.
cols.COUNTY_CODE: The county's number code. Written different ways: three digits like 001, five digits with the state like 11001, or state letters plus digits like LA099.
cols.COUNTY_NAME: The county name. Casing varies and some add the word county or municipio, so clean it before matching.
cols.STATE_CODE: The state. Usually two letters like TX, but the EPA air-monitor table uses the two-digit number code, like 01 for Alabama.
cols.STATE_NAME: The state's full name, like Texas. Some tables write it in capitals.
cols.CITY_NAME: The city name. Casing varies, and some rows say Not in a City.
cols.TEMPERATURE: The air temperature in degrees Fahrenheit when the rail incident happened.
cols.VISIBILITY_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for light conditions. The words for it are in VISIBILITY.
cols.VISIBILITY: The light conditions: Dawn, Day, Dusk or Dark.
cols.WEATHER_CONDITION_CODE: A code 1 to 6 for the weather. The words for it are in WEATHER_CONDITION.
cols.WEATHER_CONDITION: The weather at the time, like Clear, Rain, Fog or Snow.
cols.EQUIPMENT_TYPE_CODE: A code for the kind of train or equipment involved, a number or letter. Needs the rail agency's lookup.
cols.EQUIPMENT_TYPE: What kind of rail equipment was involved, like Freight Train, Yard/switching or Cut of cars. The safety table holds only N/A.
cols.TRACK_TYPE_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for the kind of track. The words for it are in TRACK_TYPE.
cols.TRACK_TYPE: The kind of track: Main, Yard, Siding or Industry.
cols.TRACK_NAME: The railroad's own name for the track, like SINGLE MAIN TRACK. Free text, spelled many ways.
cols.TRACK_CLASS: The track's safety class, a number from 1 to 6 that sets its speed limit. X means excepted track.
cols.TRAIN_SPEED: How fast the train was going, in miles per hour.
cols.TRAIN_DIRECTION_CODE: A code 1 to 4 for which way the train was heading. The words for it are in TRAIN_DIRECTION.
cols.TRAIN_DIRECTION: Which way the train was heading: North, South, East or West.
cols.FORM_54_FILED: Whether the railroad also filed a Form 54 report on the incident: Yes or No.
cols.PASSENGERS_KILLED: How many train passengers were killed. 0 in every sampled row.
cols.PASSENGERS_INJURED: How many train passengers were hurt.
cols.SPECIAL_STUDY_1: A code the rail agency uses to tag incidents for a special study, like M302. Almost always blank.
cols.SPECIAL_STUDY_2: A second special-study tag, free text like "VIDEO USED - NO". Almost always blank.
cols.NARRATIVE: A free-text account of what happened, as the reporter wrote it. Often in capitals with abbreviations.
cols.REPORT_KEY: A row ID for the rail incident report, built by gluing the railroad code, its own report number and the year and month together.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_CLASS: The size class of the railroad that filed the report: Class I is the big ones, Class III the small ones. Some rows say Not Assigned.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SMT_GROUPING: Which federal rail safety team the reporting railroad falls under, like SMT-5 - BNSF. Not Assigned shows up.
cols.REPORTING_PARENT_RAILROAD_CODE: The short code for the parent railroad of the company that filed the report, like BNSF or CSX.
cols.REPORTING_PARENT_RAILROAD_NAME: The full name of the parent railroad of the company that filed the report, like BNSF Railway Company.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_HOLDING_COMPANY: The company that owns the railroad that filed the report, like Genesee & Wyoming or BNSF Railway Company. Not Assigned shows up.
cols.URL: A web link to the record's own page at the source.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_INDIVIDUAL_CLASS: The size class of the railroad that filed the report: Class I is the big national lines, Class III the small ones. Not Assigned and Unassigned both show up.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_PASSENGER: Whether the railroad that filed the report carries passengers: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_COMMUTER: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a commuter line: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SWITCHING_TERMINAL: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a switching or terminal line that moves cars around yards: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_TOURIST: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a tourist or excursion line: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_FREIGHT: Whether the railroad that filed the report hauls freight: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
cols.REPORTING_RAILROAD_SHORT_LINE: Whether the railroad that filed the report is a small short-line railroad: Yes, or Not Assigned or Unassigned instead of No.
